article.title: Subject-matter and objectives
article.contextual_reason: Article 1 is a statement of the Regulation's purpose and legal effect (protecting natural persons' data protection rights and ensuring free movement of personal data within the Union). It imposes no operational obligation on a controller that could be evidenced in a privacy policy — there is no action, disclosure, or safeguard for a company to implement or demonstrate.

article.title: Material scope
article.contextual_reason: Article 2 defines when the Regulation applies and lists categories of processing it excludes (e.g., purely personal/household activity, law-enforcement processing, activities outside Union law). This determines whether GDPR governs a given processing activity at all — it is a threshold applicability test performed before compliance analysis, not a testable requirement a privacy policy can satisfy or fail.

article.title: Territorial scope
article.contextual_reason: Article 3 determines whether the Regulation applies to a controller or processor based on establishment location or the location/behaviour of data subjects. This is a jurisdictional applicability test, not a substantive obligation that a privacy policy document can be checked against.

article.title: Definitions
article.contextual_reason: Article 4 provides definitions of terms used throughout the Regulation (e.g., personal data, processing, controller, consent). Definitions are interpretive tools applied when assessing other articles; they do not themselves impose a requirement that a company's policy can satisfy or fail.

article.title: Principles relating to processing of personal data

requirement_groups.principle: Lawfulness, fairness, transparency, purpose limitation and minimisation
requirement_groups.requirement_summary: Data must be processed lawfully, fairly, and transparently; collected for specified, legitimate purposes and not reused incompatibly; and limited to what is necessary.

sub_obligations.legal_text: processed lawfully, fairly and in a transparent manner in relation to the data subject; collected for specified, explicit and legitimate purposes and not further processed in a manner that is incompatible with those purposes; adequate, relevant and limited to what is necessary in relation to the purposes for which they are processed
sub_obligations.plain_summary: Data must be processed on a lawful basis, fairly, and transparently; collected only for specific legitimate purposes without incompatible reuse; and limited to what is necessary for those purposes.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy establish a lawful basis, fair and transparent handling, specific purposes with compatible-only reuse, and necessity-limited collection?

assessment_rules.met_when: Lawful basis, fairness, transparency, purpose specificity, compatible reuse, and minimisation are all addressed.
assessment_rules.partially_met_when: Some but not all of these elements are addressed.
assessment_rules.not_met_when: None are addressed.
assessment_rules.conflicting_when: Policy permits unlawful, unfair, opaque, purpose-unbound, or unnecessary data practices.
assessment_rules.insufficient_evidence_when: Not enough info to assess these elements.

requirement_groups.principle: Accuracy and storage limitation
requirement_groups.requirement_summary: Data must be accurate and kept up to date, with prompt correction/erasure of inaccuracies, and retained no longer than necessary (with safeguards for extended archiving/research/statistical retention).

sub_obligations.legal_text: accurate and, where necessary, kept up to date, with every reasonable step taken to erase or rectify inaccurate data without delay; kept in a form which permits identification of data subjects for no longer than is necessary for the purposes for which the personal data are processed, except insofar as processed solely for archiving, research, or statistical purposes subject to appropriate technical and organisational measures
sub_obligations.plain_summary: Data must be accurate and promptly corrected/erased when wrong, and identifiable data kept only as long as necessary, with safeguards for any longer archival/research retention.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy commit to accuracy with prompt correction/erasure, and to necessity-based retention with safeguards for any extended retention?

assessment_rules.met_when: Accuracy/correction commitment and necessity-based retention (with safeguards where extended) are both addressed.
assessment_rules.partially_met_when: One of the two (accuracy or retention) is addressed but not the other.
assessment_rules.not_met_when: Neither is addressed.
assessment_rules.conflicting_when: Policy states inaccurate data won't be corrected, or data is retained indefinitely with no safeguard.
assessment_rules.insufficient_evidence_when: Statements too vague to assess accuracy or retention practices.

requirement_groups.principle: Integrity and confidentiality
requirement_groups.requirement_summary: Appropriate security against unauthorised/unlawful processing and accidental loss/damage.

sub_obligations.legal_text: processed in a manner that ensures appropriate security of the personal data, including protection against unauthorised or unlawful processing and against accidental loss, destruction or damage, using appropriate technical or organisational measures
sub_obligations.plain_summary: Appropriate security measures must protect data from unauthorized access, loss, or damage.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy describe appropriate technical/organisational security measures?

assessment_rules.met_when: Specific technical/organisational security measures are described.
assessment_rules.partially_met_when: General security assurance given without specifics.
assessment_rules.not_met_when: Security not addressed.
assessment_rules.conflicting_when: Policy disclaims security responsibility.
assessment_rules.insufficient_evidence_when: Security statements too generic to assess.

requirement_groups.principle: Accountability
requirement_groups.requirement_summary: Controller must be able to demonstrate compliance with Art. 5(1).

sub_obligations.legal_text: The controller shall be responsible for, and be able to demonstrate compliance with, paragraph 1 ('accountability').
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The company must be able to prove, not just claim, compliance.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy indicate records/evidence demonstrating compliance?

assessment_rules.met_when: Policy indicates evidence/documentation demonstrating compliance.
assessment_rules.partially_met_when: Compliance asserted generally with no means of demonstration.
assessment_rules.not_met_when: No accountability statement.
assessment_rules.conflicting_when: Policy disclaims any duty to demonstrate compliance.
assessment_rules.insufficient_evidence_when: How compliance is demonstrated is unaddressed.

requirement_groups.principle: Lawful basis for processing
requirement_groups.requirement_summary: Processing is lawful only if at least ONE of the legal bases in Article 6(1) applies.

sub_obligations.legal_text: the data subject has given consent to the processing of his or her personal data for one or more specific purposes
sub_obligations.plain_summary: Processing based on the person's consent for specific purposes.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy identify consent as a lawful basis for processing?

sub_obligations.legal_text: processing is necessary for the performance of a contract to which the data subject is party, or in order to take steps at the request of the data subject prior to entering into a contract; or processing is necessary for compliance with a legal obligation to which the controller is subject
sub_obligations.plain_summary: Processing needed to perform (or enter into) a contract with the person, or to comply with a legal requirement.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy identify contract performance/pre-contractual steps or legal-obligation compliance as a lawful basis for processing?

sub_obligations.legal_text: processing is necessary in order to protect the vital interests of the data subject or of another natural person; or processing is necessary for the performance of a task carried out in the public interest or in the exercise of official authority vested in the controller
sub_obligations.plain_summary: Processing needed to protect someone's life/vital interests, or to carry out a public-interest task or official authority, where applicable.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy identify vital-interest protection or public-interest/official-authority tasks as a lawful basis, where applicable?

sub_obligations.legal_text: processing is necessary for the purposes of the legitimate interests pursued by the controller or by a third party, except where such interests are overridden by the interests or fundamental rights and freedoms of the data subject
sub_obligations.plain_summary: Processing based on the company's or a third party's legitimate interests, balanced against the person's rights.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy identify legitimate interests as a lawful basis and describe how those interests are balanced against the data subject's rights?

assessment_rules.met_when: The policy documents at least ONE valid, clearly applicable lawful basis for each relevant processing activity.
assessment_rules.partially_met_when: A lawful basis is referenced but is vague or inconsistently applied.
assessment_rules.not_met_when: No lawful basis is identified for relevant processing.
assessment_rules.conflicting_when: The policy processes data without any identifiable lawful basis, or relies on legitimate interests for processing carried out by a public authority in performance of its tasks.
assessment_rules.insufficient_evidence_when: The policy does not provide enough information to determine which lawful basis applies.

requirement_groups.principle: Legal-basis grounding for legal-obligation and public-task processing
requirement_groups.requirement_summary: Where processing relies on the legal-obligation or public-task grounds, the basis for that processing must be laid down by Union or Member State law meeting an objective of public interest and proportionate to the aim pursued.
requirement_groups.applicability_condition: Applies only where the controller relies on Article 6(1)(c) (legal obligation) or 6(1)(e) (public task) as its lawful basis.

sub_obligations.legal_text: The basis for the processing referred to in point (c) and (e) of paragraph 1 shall be laid down by Union law; or Member State law to which the controller is subject.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: If relying on legal obligation or public task as the basis, that basis must come from an actual Union or Member State law.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Where legal-obligation or public-task grounds are relied on, does the policy identify the specific law establishing that basis?

expected_evidence: Reference to specific statutes underpinning legal-obligation or public-task processing

assessment_rules.met_when: Where legal-obligation or public-task grounds are relied on, the policy identifies the specific applicable law establishing that basis.
assessment_rules.partially_met_when: The ground is stated generically (e.g., 'as required by law') without identifying the specific law.
assessment_rules.not_met_when: The ground is relied on with no reference to any underlying law.
assessment_rules.conflicting_when: The policy cites a law that does not plausibly establish the processing described.
assessment_rules.insufficient_evidence_when: It cannot be determined whether legal-obligation or public-task grounds are relied on.

requirement_groups.principle: Compatibility assessment for further processing on a new purpose
requirement_groups.requirement_summary: Where further processing for a new purpose is not based on consent or a law safeguarding Article 23(1) objectives, the controller must consider specified factors (link to original purpose, collection context, nature of data, consequences for data subjects, and safeguards) to assess compatibility with the original purpose.
requirement_groups.applicability_condition: Applies only where the controller further processes data for a new purpose without relying on consent or an Article 23(1)-compliant law.

sub_obligations.legal_text: take into account, inter alia: any link between the purposes...the context in which the personal data have been collected...the nature of the personal data...the possible consequences of the intended further processing...the existence of appropriate safeguards
sub_obligations.plain_summary: Before reusing data for a new purpose without consent or a qualifying law, the company must weigh factors like the link to the original purpose, context of collection, sensitivity of the data, likely consequences, and any safeguards in place.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Where further processing occurs without consent or a qualifying law, does the policy describe a compatibility assessment considering these factors?

assessment_rules.met_when: Where applicable, the policy describes a compatibility assessment addressing ALL the listed factors before further processing for a new purpose.
assessment_rules.partially_met_when: A compatibility assessment is mentioned but does not address most of the listed factors.
assessment_rules.not_met_when: The policy allows repurposing of data with no compatibility assessment described.
assessment_rules.conflicting_when: The policy states data will be repurposed regardless of compatibility with original purposes.
assessment_rules.insufficient_evidence_when: It cannot be determined whether the controller repurposes data outside of consent or a qualifying law.

requirement_groups.principle: Ability to demonstrate consent
requirement_groups.requirement_summary: Where processing is based on consent, the controller must be able to demonstrate that the data subject consented.
requirement_groups.applicability_condition: Applies only where consent is the lawful basis relied on.

sub_obligations.legal_text: the controller shall be able to demonstrate that the data subject has consented to processing of his or her personal data
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The company must be able to prove that a person actually consented.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Where consent is relied on, does the policy describe how consent is recorded or evidenced?

assessment_rules.met_when: Where consent is used as a basis, the policy describes a mechanism for recording or evidencing that consent was given.
assessment_rules.partially_met_when: Consent is referenced as a basis but no record-keeping mechanism is described.
assessment_rules.not_met_when: Consent is used as a basis with no means described to demonstrate it was obtained.
assessment_rules.conflicting_when: The policy states consent records are not retained.
assessment_rules.insufficient_evidence_when: It cannot be determined whether consent is used as a lawful basis.

requirement_groups.principle: Clear presentation of consent requests
requirement_groups.requirement_summary: Where consent is requested within a written declaration covering other matters, the request must be presented clearly distinguishable, intelligible, and in plain language, and any infringing part of the declaration is not binding.
requirement_groups.applicability_condition: Applies where a consent request is bundled within a broader written declaration.

sub_obligations.legal_text: the request for consent shall be presented in a manner which is clearly distinguishable from the other matters, in an intelligible and easily accessible form, using clear and plain language
sub_obligations.plain_summary: A consent request bundled with other terms must stand out clearly and be written in plain, accessible language.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Where consent is requested alongside other terms, is it presented distinguishably, intelligibly, and in plain language?

sub_obligations.legal_text: Any part of such a declaration which constitutes an infringement of this Regulation shall not be binding.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: Any part of the declaration that violates GDPR doesn't count as valid consent.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy acknowledge that consent obtained through non-compliant bundled declarations is not binding?

assessment_rules.met_when: Where consent is bundled with other matters, the policy satisfies ALL sub-obligations: a distinguishable, plain-language request, and acknowledgment that non-compliant parts are not binding.
assessment_rules.partially_met_when: A clear presentation is described but the non-binding-infringement acknowledgment is absent.
assessment_rules.not_met_when: Consent requests are not distinguished from other terms at all.
assessment_rules.conflicting_when: The policy states consent bundled within lengthy terms is treated as valid regardless of clarity.
assessment_rules.insufficient_evidence_when: It cannot be determined whether consent requests are bundled with other declarations.

requirement_groups.principle: Right to withdraw consent
requirement_groups.requirement_summary: The data subject may withdraw consent at any time without affecting the lawfulness of prior processing, must be informed of this right before consenting, and withdrawal must be as easy as giving consent.
requirement_groups.applicability_condition: Applies only where consent is the lawful basis relied on.

sub_obligations.legal_text: The data subject shall have the right to withdraw his or her consent at any time.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: People can withdraw their consent whenever they want.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy confirm the right to withdraw consent at any time?

sub_obligations.legal_text: The withdrawal of consent shall not affect the lawfulness of processing based on consent before its withdrawal.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: Withdrawing consent doesn't undo the lawfulness of past processing done under that consent.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy confirm that withdrawal doesn't affect the lawfulness of prior consent-based processing?

sub_obligations.legal_text: Prior to giving consent, the data subject shall be informed thereof.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: People must be told about their withdrawal right before they give consent.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy commit to informing the data subject of the withdrawal right before they consent?

sub_obligations.legal_text: It shall be as easy to withdraw as to give consent.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: Withdrawing consent must be just as simple as giving it in the first place.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy confirm that withdrawing consent is as easy as giving it?

assessment_rules.met_when: The policy satisfies ALL sub-obligations: withdrawal is available at any time, does not retroactively affect prior processing lawfulness, is disclosed before consent is given, and is as easy as giving consent.
assessment_rules.partially_met_when: Withdrawal is available but one or more of the other conditions (prior notice, ease of withdrawal, non-retroactivity) is missing.
assessment_rules.not_met_when: No withdrawal mechanism is described despite consent being used as a basis.
assessment_rules.conflicting_when: The policy makes withdrawal materially harder than giving consent (e.g., requiring a phone call to withdraw online-given consent).
assessment_rules.insufficient_evidence_when: It cannot be determined whether consent is used as a lawful basis or how withdrawal works.

requirement_groups.principle: Freely given consent assessment
requirement_groups.requirement_summary: In assessing whether consent is freely given, utmost account must be taken of whether contract performance, including service provision, is made conditional on consent to processing not necessary for that contract.
requirement_groups.applicability_condition: Applies where consent is sought in connection with the performance of a contract or provision of a service.

sub_obligations.legal_text: utmost account shall be taken of whether, inter alia, the performance of a contract...is conditional on consent to the processing of personal data that is not necessary for the performance of that contract
sub_obligations.plain_summary: Consent isn't freely given if a person must agree to unnecessary data processing just to get a contract or service.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy avoid conditioning contract or service performance on consent to processing not necessary for that contract?

expected_evidence: Statement distinguishing necessary processing from consent-based add-ons

assessment_rules.met_when: The policy confirms that contract or service performance is not made conditional on consent to processing unnecessary for that contract.
assessment_rules.partially_met_when: The policy separates necessary and optional processing but doesn't explicitly disclaim conditioning service on unnecessary consent.
assessment_rules.not_met_when: The policy does not address the relationship between contract performance and consent to unrelated processing.
assessment_rules.conflicting_when: The policy conditions access to a service on consent to processing unrelated to delivering that service.
assessment_rules.insufficient_evidence_when: It cannot be determined whether consent is bundled with contract or service performance.

article.title: Conditions applicable to child's consent in relation to information society services

requirement_groups.principle: Age threshold for a child's valid consent
requirement_groups.requirement_summary: Where consent is the basis for offering information society services directly to a child, processing is lawful if the child is at least 16 (or a lower Member State-set age, not below 13); below that age, processing is lawful only with parental consent or authorisation.
requirement_groups.applicability_condition: Applies only where the controller offers information society services directly to a child and relies on consent under Article 6(1)(a).

sub_obligations.legal_text: the processing of the personal data of a child shall be lawful where the child is at least 16 years old
sub_obligations.plain_summary: A child aged 16 or older (or the applicable lower age) can validly consent themselves.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Where information society services are offered to children, does the policy apply the correct age threshold for valid self-consent?

sub_obligations.legal_text: Where the child is below the age of 16 years, such processing shall be lawful only if and to the extent that consent is given or authorised by the holder of parental responsibility over the child. Member States may provide by law for a lower age...not below 13 years.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: For children below the applicable age threshold, a parent or guardian must give or authorise consent.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy require parental consent or authorisation for children below the applicable age threshold?

assessment_rules.met_when: Where information society services are offered directly to children on a consent basis, the policy satisfies ALL sub-obligations: applying the correct age threshold and requiring parental consent below it.
assessment_rules.partially_met_when: An age threshold is applied but no parental consent mechanism is described for younger children.
assessment_rules.not_met_when: No age-based consent distinction is made despite offering services to children.
assessment_rules.conflicting_when: The policy accepts self-consent from children below the applicable threshold without parental involvement.
assessment_rules.insufficient_evidence_when: It cannot be determined whether the controller offers information society services directly to children.

requirement_groups.principle: Reasonable efforts to verify parental consent
requirement_groups.requirement_summary: The controller must make reasonable efforts to verify that consent for a child below the applicable age was given or authorised by the holder of parental responsibility, taking into account available technology.
requirement_groups.applicability_condition: Applies only where parental consent is relied on for a child below the applicable age threshold.

sub_obligations.legal_text: The controller shall make reasonable efforts to verify in such cases that consent is given or authorised by the holder of parental responsibility over the child, taking into consideration available technology.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The company must make a reasonable effort, using available technology, to check that a parent really gave the consent.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy describe reasonable, technology-appropriate efforts to verify parental consent?

assessment_rules.met_when: The policy describes reasonable, technology-appropriate steps to verify parental consent where relied upon.
assessment_rules.partially_met_when: Parental consent is collected but no verification method is described.
assessment_rules.not_met_when: No verification effort is described despite relying on parental consent.
assessment_rules.conflicting_when: The policy accepts unverified self-declared parental consent with no further check.
assessment_rules.insufficient_evidence_when: It cannot be determined whether the controller relies on parental consent.

article.title: Processing of special categories of personal data

requirement_groups.principle: Prohibition on processing special category data
requirement_groups.requirement_summary: Processing of data revealing racial/ethnic origin, political opinions, religious/philosophical beliefs, trade union membership, genetic data, biometric data used for unique identification, health data, or data on sex life/sexual orientation is prohibited by default.

sub_obligations.legal_text: Processing of personal data revealing racial or ethnic origin, political opinions, religious or philosophical beliefs, or trade union membership, and the processing of genetic data, biometric data for the purpose of uniquely identifying a natural person, data concerning health or data concerning a natural person's sex life or sexual orientation shall be prohibited.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: Special category data is off-limits by default unless an exception applies.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy acknowledge that special category data is prohibited from processing absent an applicable exception?

assessment_rules.met_when: The policy acknowledges the default prohibition on processing special category data and processes such data only pursuant to a documented exception (see group 9.2).
assessment_rules.partially_met_when: The policy processes special category data without clearly acknowledging the default prohibition, though an exception basis is documented elsewhere.
assessment_rules.not_met_when: The policy does not address special category data at all despite apparently processing it.
assessment_rules.conflicting_when: The policy processes special category data with no exception identified.
assessment_rules.insufficient_evidence_when: It cannot be determined whether the controller processes special category data.

requirement_groups.principle: Exceptions permitting special category data processing
requirement_groups.requirement_summary: The prohibition does not apply if at least ONE of the listed exceptions applies (e.g., explicit consent, employment/social security law obligations, vital interests, not-for-profit body processing of members' data, manifestly public data, legal claims, substantial public interest, health/social care purposes, public health, or archiving/research/statistical purposes).
requirement_groups.applicability_condition: Applies only where the controller processes special category data.

sub_obligations.legal_text: the data subject has given explicit consent to the processing of those personal data for one or more specified purposes
sub_obligations.plain_summary: Processing is allowed with the person's explicit consent for specific purposes.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy identify explicit consent as a basis for processing special category data, where applicable?

sub_obligations.legal_text: processing is necessary for the purposes of carrying out the obligations and exercising specific rights of the controller or of the data subject in the field of employment and social security and social protection law
sub_obligations.plain_summary: Processing allowed for employment, social security, or social protection law obligations with appropriate safeguards.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy identify employment/social security law obligations as a basis, where applicable?

sub_obligations.legal_text: processing is necessary to protect the vital interests of the data subject or of another natural person where the data subject is physically or legally incapable of giving consent
sub_obligations.plain_summary: Processing allowed to protect someone's vital interests when they can't consent.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy identify protection of vital interests as a basis, where applicable?

sub_obligations.legal_text: processing is carried out in the course of its legitimate activities with appropriate safeguards by a foundation, association or any other not-for-profit body with a political, philosophical, religious or trade union aim...relates solely to the members or to former members
sub_obligations.plain_summary: Not-for-profit bodies can process members'/former members' data related to their aims, with safeguards and without external disclosure.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Where applicable, does the policy describe not-for-profit membership-data processing with appropriate safeguards?

sub_obligations.legal_text: processing relates to personal data which are manifestly made public by the data subject
sub_obligations.plain_summary: Processing is allowed for data the person has clearly made public themselves.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy identify manifestly public data as a basis, where applicable?

sub_obligations.legal_text: processing is necessary for the establishment, exercise or defence of legal claims or whenever courts are acting in their judicial capacity
sub_obligations.plain_summary: Processing is allowed for legal claims or judicial proceedings.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy identify legal claims/judicial capacity as a basis, where applicable?

sub_obligations.legal_text: processing is necessary for reasons of substantial public interest, on the basis of Union or Member State law
sub_obligations.plain_summary: Processing is allowed for substantial public interest reasons grounded in law.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy identify substantial public interest under law as a basis, where applicable?

sub_obligations.legal_text: processing is necessary for the purposes of preventive or occupational medicine...medical diagnosis, the provision of health or social care or treatment or the management of health or social care systems
sub_obligations.plain_summary: Processing is allowed for healthcare, occupational medicine, or health/social care system management purposes.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy identify healthcare or health/social care management purposes as a basis, where applicable?

sub_obligations.legal_text: processing is necessary for reasons of public interest in the area of public health
sub_obligations.plain_summary: Processing is allowed for public health reasons such as protecting against cross-border health threats.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy identify public health reasons as a basis, where applicable?

sub_obligations.legal_text: processing is necessary for archiving purposes in the public interest, scientific or historical research purposes or statistical purposes in accordance with Article 89(1)
sub_obligations.plain_summary: Processing is allowed for archiving, research, or statistical purposes with appropriate safeguards.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy identify archiving/research/statistical purposes as a basis, where applicable?

assessment_rules.met_when: Where special category data is processed, the policy documents AT LEAST ONE applicable exception with a consistent factual basis.
assessment_rules.partially_met_when: An exception is invoked but is vague or lacks the safeguards required by that specific exception.
assessment_rules.not_met_when: Special category data is processed with no exception identified.
assessment_rules.conflicting_when: The policy invokes an exception inconsistent with the facts described (e.g., claims explicit consent but describes only implicit opt-out).
assessment_rules.insufficient_evidence_when: It cannot be determined whether the controller processes special category data or which exception applies.

requirement_groups.principle: Professional secrecy safeguard for health/social care processing
requirement_groups.requirement_summary: Special category data processed under the health/social care exception (9(2)(h)) may only be processed by or under the responsibility of a professional subject to an obligation of professional secrecy, or another person also subject to a secrecy obligation.
requirement_groups.applicability_condition: Applies only where the controller relies on Article 9(2)(h) (health/social care purposes) as its exception.

sub_obligations.legal_text: Personal data referred to in paragraph 1 may be processed for the purposes referred to in point (h) of paragraph 2 when those data are processed by or under the responsibility of a professional subject to the obligation of professional secrecy...or by another person also subject to an obligation of secrecy
sub_obligations.plain_summary: Health-related sensitive data processed under the healthcare exception must be handled by, or under, someone bound by professional secrecy.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Where the healthcare exception is relied on, does the policy confirm data is processed by or under a professional or other person bound by secrecy obligations?

expected_evidence: Professional secrecy/confidentiality obligation statement for health data handlers

assessment_rules.met_when: Where the health/social care exception is relied on, the policy confirms processing occurs by or under the responsibility of someone bound by a professional secrecy obligation.
assessment_rules.partially_met_when: The healthcare exception is relied on but no secrecy-obligation safeguard is described.
assessment_rules.not_met_when: The healthcare exception is relied on with no reference to secrecy obligations at all.
assessment_rules.conflicting_when: The policy allows health data handling by personnel expressly not bound by any secrecy obligation.
assessment_rules.insufficient_evidence_when: It cannot be determined whether the controller relies on the health/social care exception.

article.title: Processing of personal data relating to criminal convictions and offences

requirement_groups.principle: Authority basis for processing criminal conviction/offence data
requirement_groups.requirement_summary: Processing of criminal conviction and offence data may be carried out only under the control of official authority, or when authorised by Union or Member State law providing appropriate safeguards; any comprehensive register of criminal convictions must be kept only under official authority control.
requirement_groups.applicability_condition: Applies only where the controller processes personal data relating to criminal convictions, offences, or related security measures.

sub_obligations.legal_text: shall be carried out only under the control of official authority
sub_obligations.plain_summary: Criminal conviction data can be processed under the control of an official authority.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Where criminal conviction data is processed, does the policy indicate this occurs under the control of official authority?

sub_obligations.legal_text: or when the processing is authorised by Union or Member State law providing for appropriate safeguards for the rights and freedoms of data subjects
sub_obligations.plain_summary: Alternatively, it can be processed when authorised by law that provides adequate safeguards.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Where criminal conviction data is processed outside official authority control, does the policy identify authorising law and describe appropriate safeguards?

expected_evidence: Criminal records handling basis and safeguards documentation

assessment_rules.met_when: Where criminal conviction/offence data is processed, the policy documents AT LEAST ONE valid basis: official authority control or law-authorised processing with appropriate safeguards.
assessment_rules.partially_met_when: A basis is referenced but safeguards are not described where processing occurs outside official authority control.
assessment_rules.not_met_when: Criminal conviction/offence data is processed with no basis identified.
assessment_rules.conflicting_when: The policy processes such data outside official authority control with no legal authorisation or safeguards.
assessment_rules.insufficient_evidence_when: It cannot be determined whether the controller processes criminal conviction or offence data.

requirement_groups.principle: Comprehensive criminal conviction registers
requirement_groups.requirement_summary: Any comprehensive register of criminal convictions must be kept only under the control of official authority.
requirement_groups.applicability_condition: Applies only where the controller maintains a comprehensive register of criminal convictions.

sub_obligations.legal_text: Any comprehensive register of criminal convictions shall be kept only under the control of official authority.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: A full register of criminal convictions can only be maintained under official authority control.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Where a comprehensive criminal conviction register is maintained, does the policy confirm it is kept under official authority control?

assessment_rules.met_when: Where a comprehensive criminal conviction register is maintained, the policy confirms it is kept under official authority control.
assessment_rules.partially_met_when: A register is described without clarity on whether official authority control applies.
assessment_rules.not_met_when: A comprehensive register is maintained without any official authority control described.
assessment_rules.conflicting_when: The policy states such a register is maintained by the controller without any official authority oversight.
assessment_rules.insufficient_evidence_when: It cannot be determined whether the controller maintains a comprehensive criminal conviction register.

article.title: Processing which does not require identification

requirement_groups.principle: No obligation to acquire identifying information solely for GDPR compliance
requirement_groups.requirement_summary: Where a controller's processing purposes do not or no longer require identifying a data subject, the controller is not obliged to maintain, acquire, or process additional information solely to identify the data subject for GDPR compliance purposes.
requirement_groups.applicability_condition: Applies only where the controller's processing purposes do not require identification of the data subject.

sub_obligations.legal_text: the controller shall not be obliged to maintain, acquire or process additional information in order to identify the data subject for the sole purpose of complying with this Regulation
sub_obligations.plain_summary: If the company doesn't need to know who someone is for its processing, it doesn't have to go out of its way to identify them just to comply with GDPR.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Where identification is not required for processing, does the policy confirm the company will not acquire additional identifying data solely for compliance purposes?

expected_evidence: Statement on non-identifying or anonymised processing practices

assessment_rules.met_when: Where identification is not required for the controller's processing, the policy confirms it will not acquire additional identifying information solely for GDPR compliance.
assessment_rules.partially_met_when: The policy describes non-identifying processing but doesn't clarify whether extra identifying data would be sought for compliance purposes.
assessment_rules.not_met_when: The policy is silent on this point despite processing that does not require identification.
assessment_rules.conflicting_when: The policy states it will acquire identifying data purely to facilitate rights requests even when not otherwise needed for processing.
assessment_rules.insufficient_evidence_when: It cannot be determined whether the controller conducts any processing that does not require identification.

requirement_groups.principle: Notification and limited rights applicability where identification is not possible
requirement_groups.requirement_summary: Where the controller can demonstrate it cannot identify the data subject, it must inform the data subject accordingly if possible, and the rights under Articles 15-20 do not apply unless the data subject provides additional information enabling identification for exercising those rights.
requirement_groups.applicability_condition: Applies only where the controller is unable to identify the data subject in the Article 11(1) circumstances.

sub_obligations.legal_text: the controller shall inform the data subject accordingly, if possible
sub_obligations.plain_summary: If the company can't identify someone, it should tell them so, if it's able to.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Where the controller cannot identify a data subject, does the policy commit to informing them of this, where possible?

sub_obligations.legal_text: In such cases, Articles 15 to 20 shall not apply except where the data subject, for the purpose of exercising his or her rights under those articles, provides additional information enabling his or her identification.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: Rights like access and portability don't apply if the company can't identify the person, unless the person provides more information to enable identification.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy explain that access, rectification, erasure, restriction, and portability rights do not apply where identification isn't possible, unless the data subject provides identifying information?

expected_evidence: Statement on rights limitations for non-identifiable data

assessment_rules.met_when: The policy satisfies ALL applicable sub-obligations: it commits to notifying data subjects where identification is not possible, and correctly explains the limited applicability of Articles 15-20 absent additional identifying information.
assessment_rules.partially_met_when: The rights-limitation explanation is present but the notification commitment is missing, or vice versa.
assessment_rules.not_met_when: The policy does not address this scenario at all despite processing data it cannot link to identifiable individuals.
assessment_rules.conflicting_when: The policy claims to honor Articles 15-20 requests without any identification possible, which is not feasible in practice, or denies data subjects the option to provide identifying information to exercise their rights.
assessment_rules.insufficient_evidence_when: It cannot be determined whether the controller processes data it cannot link to identifiable individuals.

article.title: Transparent information, communication and modalities for the exercise of the rights of the data subject

requirement_groups.principle: Clear and accessible form of information
requirement_groups.requirement_summary: Information provided to data subjects must be presented concisely, transparently, intelligibly, and accessibly, using plain language, with special care when addressed to children.

sub_obligations.legal_text: concise, transparent, intelligible and easily accessible form, using clear and plain language
sub_obligations.plain_summary: Information must be presented briefly, clearly, and in plain language that is easy to access and understand.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy present information in a concise, transparent, and easily accessible way using clear and plain language?

sub_obligations.legal_text: in particular for any information addressed specifically to a child
sub_obligations.plain_summary: Extra care must be taken with clarity and simplicity when information is directed specifically at children.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy use simplified or child-appropriate language in any sections addressed specifically to children?

assessment_rules.met_when: The policy satisfies ALL sub-obligations: it is written concisely and in plain, accessible language, and takes distinct care with clarity where addressing children.
assessment_rules.partially_met_when: The policy is generally clear and accessible but does not address the child-specific language requirement, or vice versa.
assessment_rules.not_met_when: The policy is dense, legalistic, or inaccessible and makes no attempt at plain-language or child-appropriate communication.
assessment_rules.conflicting_when: The policy explicitly states it uses complex legal language without simplification, or treats children's data the same as adults' with no accommodation.
assessment_rules.insufficient_evidence_when: The policy does not describe its communication style or whether it addresses children at all.

requirement_groups.principle: Modality of providing information
requirement_groups.requirement_summary: Information must be provided in writing or another suitable means, including electronically where appropriate; it may also be given orally on request once the data subject's identity is verified by other means.

sub_obligations.legal_text: The information shall be provided in writing, or by other means, including, where appropriate, by electronic means.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: Information can be given in writing or another suitable method, including electronically.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy state that information is provided in writing or by other means, including electronic means where appropriate?

sub_obligations.legal_text: When requested by the data subject, the information may be provided orally, provided that the identity of the data subject is proven by other means.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: If the person asks, information can be given orally, but only after verifying their identity through another method.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy allow oral provision of information upon request, subject to identity verification?

assessment_rules.met_when: The policy documents AT LEAST ONE valid modality for providing information (written/electronic as the default, or oral with identity verification as an option).
assessment_rules.partially_met_when: A delivery modality is mentioned but lacks detail (e.g., electronic delivery mentioned without any identity-verification process for oral requests).
assessment_rules.not_met_when: The policy does not describe any method by which information is delivered to data subjects.
assessment_rules.conflicting_when: The policy states information will only be provided orally with no identity verification safeguard.
assessment_rules.insufficient_evidence_when: The policy is silent on how information is actually delivered to data subjects.

requirement_groups.principle: Facilitating exercise of data subject rights
requirement_groups.requirement_summary: Controllers must facilitate the exercise of rights under Articles 15-22 and cannot refuse to act on a request except where, in Article 11(2) situations, they cannot identify the data subject.
requirement_groups.applicability_condition: The non-refusal limitation specifically concerns processing situations falling under Article 11(2), where identification is not otherwise required for the processing.

sub_obligations.legal_text: The controller shall facilitate the exercise of data subject rights under Articles 15 to 22.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The company must make it easy for people to exercise their data protection rights.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy describe mechanisms that make it easy for individuals to exercise their rights (access, rectification, erasure, etc.)?

sub_obligations.legal_text: the controller shall not refuse to act on the request of the data subject for exercising his or her rights under Articles 15 to 22, unless the controller demonstrates that it is not in a position to identify the data subject
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The company cannot refuse a rights request unless it genuinely cannot identify who is making it.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy confirm that rights requests are only refused when the requester's identity cannot be established?

assessment_rules.met_when: The policy satisfies ALL sub-obligations: it describes accessible mechanisms for exercising rights and confirms requests are not refused except for genuine identification failure.
assessment_rules.partially_met_when: The policy describes rights mechanisms but does not address the limited grounds for refusal, or vice versa.
assessment_rules.not_met_when: The policy provides no clear mechanism for exercising rights and/or allows broad refusal of requests.
assessment_rules.conflicting_when: The policy states requests may be refused for reasons other than identification failure.
assessment_rules.insufficient_evidence_when: The policy does not describe how rights requests are handled or refused.

requirement_groups.principle: Timeframe and format for responding to rights requests
requirement_groups.requirement_summary: The controller must act on a request without undue delay and within one month (extendable by two further months with notice and reasons), and generally reply electronically to electronic requests.

sub_obligations.legal_text: without undue delay and in any event within one month of receipt of the request
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The company must respond within one month, sooner if possible.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy commit to responding to rights requests without undue delay and within one month?

sub_obligations.legal_text: That period may be extended by two further months where necessary, taking into account the complexity and number of the requests.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The response window can be extended by up to two extra months for complex or numerous requests.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy describe a possible extension of up to two months for complex or numerous requests?

sub_obligations.legal_text: The controller shall inform the data subject of any such extension within one month of receipt of the request, together with the reasons for the delay.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: If extending the deadline, the company must notify the person within the first month and explain why.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy state that the data subject will be notified of any extension and its reasons within the first month?

sub_obligations.legal_text: Where the data subject makes the request by electronic form means, the information shall be provided by electronic means where possible, unless otherwise requested by the data subject.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: Requests made electronically will generally get an electronic response unless the person asks otherwise.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy state that electronic requests are answered electronically unless the requester asks otherwise?

assessment_rules.met_when: The policy satisfies ALL sub-obligations: a one-month default deadline, a described extension process with notice and reasons, and electronic responses to electronic requests by default.
assessment_rules.partially_met_when: A deadline is stated but the extension process or electronic-response default is missing or unclear.
assessment_rules.not_met_when: No response deadline or timeframe is described at all.
assessment_rules.conflicting_when: The policy states a response deadline longer than three months, or that extensions are made without notifying the data subject.
assessment_rules.insufficient_evidence_when: The policy does not specify a timeframe for responding to requests.

requirement_groups.principle: Notification when controller does not act on a request
requirement_groups.requirement_summary: If the controller does not act on a request, it must inform the data subject without delay and within one month, giving reasons and informing them of the right to complain to a supervisory authority or seek a judicial remedy.
requirement_groups.applicability_condition: Applies when the controller decides not to take action on a data subject rights request.

sub_obligations.legal_text: the controller shall inform the data subject without delay and at the latest within one month of receipt of the request of the reasons for not taking action
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The company must promptly, and within a month, explain why it is not acting on the request.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy commit to informing requesters within one month if their request will not be actioned, including the reasons?

sub_obligations.legal_text: on the possibility of lodging a complaint with a supervisory authority and seeking a judicial remedy
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The company must tell the person they can complain to a supervisory authority or go to court.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy inform data subjects of their right to complain to a supervisory authority or seek a judicial remedy when a request is refused?

assessment_rules.met_when: The policy satisfies ALL sub-obligations: refusal reasons are communicated within one month and the data subject is told of complaint and judicial remedy options.
assessment_rules.partially_met_when: Reasons for refusal are communicated but complaint/remedy information is omitted, or vice versa.
assessment_rules.not_met_when: The policy does not describe any process for notifying data subjects when a request is refused.
assessment_rules.conflicting_when: The policy states that refused requests receive no explanation or information about further recourse.
assessment_rules.insufficient_evidence_when: The policy does not address what happens when a request is not actioned.

requirement_groups.principle: Free-of-charge provision of information
requirement_groups.requirement_summary: Information under Articles 13 and 14, and communications/actions under Articles 15-22 and 34, must generally be provided free of charge.

sub_obligations.legal_text: Information provided under Articles 13 and 14 and any communication and any actions taken under Articles 15 to 22 and 34 shall be provided free of charge.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: Standard information and rights-request responses must not be charged for.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy confirm that data subject requests and related disclosures are provided free of charge?

expected_evidence: Fee/pricing statements in the rights-request section

assessment_rules.met_when: The policy confirms information and standard rights-request responses are provided free of charge.
assessment_rules.partially_met_when: The policy implies free provision but is ambiguous about whether any charges could apply.
assessment_rules.not_met_when: The policy does not mention cost or implies fees apply to all requests.
assessment_rules.conflicting_when: The policy states a fee applies to standard (non-excessive) requests.
assessment_rules.insufficient_evidence_when: The policy does not address cost of providing information or handling requests.

requirement_groups.principle: Fee or refusal for manifestly unfounded or excessive requests
requirement_groups.requirement_summary: For manifestly unfounded or excessive requests, particularly repetitive ones, the controller may charge a reasonable administrative fee or refuse to act, but must be able to demonstrate the unfounded or excessive character of the request.
requirement_groups.applicability_condition: Applies only where a specific data subject request is manifestly unfounded or excessive, in particular due to its repetitive character.

sub_obligations.legal_text: charge a reasonable fee taking into account the administrative costs of providing the information or communication or taking the action requested
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The company may charge a reasonable fee based on administrative costs.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy describe charging a reasonable administrative fee for manifestly unfounded or excessive requests?

sub_obligations.legal_text: refuse to act on the request
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The company may decline to act on the request instead of charging a fee.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy describe the option to refuse manifestly unfounded or excessive requests?

assessment_rules.met_when: The policy documents AT LEAST ONE of the two permitted responses (reasonable fee or refusal) to manifestly unfounded/excessive requests, AND indicates the controller bears the burden of justifying that characterization.
assessment_rules.partially_met_when: A fee or refusal option is mentioned but without acknowledging the controller's burden to justify the unfounded/excessive characterization.
assessment_rules.not_met_when: The policy does not address how manifestly unfounded or excessive requests are handled.
assessment_rules.conflicting_when: The policy states that fees apply to requests generally, without limiting this to unfounded/excessive cases, or applies these measures without any justification standard.
assessment_rules.insufficient_evidence_when: The policy does not describe treatment of repetitive, unfounded, or excessive requests.

requirement_groups.principle: Additional identity verification
requirement_groups.requirement_summary: Where the controller has reasonable doubts about the identity of a person making a request under Articles 15-21, it may request additional information to confirm identity.
requirement_groups.applicability_condition: Applies where the controller has reasonable doubts concerning the identity of the person making a rights request under Articles 15 to 21.

sub_obligations.legal_text: the controller may request the provision of additional information necessary to confirm the identity of the data subject
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The company can ask for further proof of identity if it has genuine doubts about who is making the request.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy describe a process for requesting additional identity verification when there is reasonable doubt about a requester's identity?

expected_evidence: Identity verification procedures for rights requests

assessment_rules.met_when: The policy describes a proportionate process for requesting additional identity information when there is reasonable doubt about a requester's identity.
assessment_rules.partially_met_when: Identity verification is mentioned generally but no criteria or proportionality (reasonable doubt) is described.
assessment_rules.not_met_when: The policy has no identity verification process at all.
assessment_rules.conflicting_when: The policy requires excessive identity verification for all requests regardless of doubt, effectively acting as a barrier to rights exercise.
assessment_rules.insufficient_evidence_when: The policy does not address identity verification procedures.

requirement_groups.principle: Use of standardised icons
requirement_groups.requirement_summary: Information under Articles 13 and 14 may optionally be supplemented with standardised icons giving a visible overview of processing; where used electronically, such icons must be machine-readable.
requirement_groups.applicability_condition: Applies only if the controller chooses to use standardised icons to summarise privacy information.

sub_obligations.legal_text: provided in combination with standardised icons in order to give in an easily visible, intelligible and clearly legible manner a meaningful overview of the intended processing
sub_obligations.plain_summary: Icons can be used alongside text to give a clear, visible summary of how data is processed.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy use standardised icons to summarise processing information?

sub_obligations.legal_text: Where the icons are presented electronically they shall be machine-readable.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: Any icons shown online must also be readable by machines or software.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: If icons are used electronically, are they implemented in a machine-readable format?

assessment_rules.met_when: Where icons are used, the policy satisfies ALL sub-obligations: icons give a clear visible overview and, if electronic, are machine-readable.
assessment_rules.partially_met_when: Icons are used but machine-readability (for electronic versions) is not addressed.
assessment_rules.not_met_when: Icons are used but are unclear, misleading, or not machine-readable when presented electronically.
assessment_rules.conflicting_when: Not applicable in typical cases; would require an explicit statement that icons are used but deliberately not machine-readable.
assessment_rules.insufficient_evidence_when: The policy does not indicate whether standardised icons are used at all (this group is not applicable if icons are not used).

article.title: Information to be provided where personal data are collected from the data subject

requirement_groups.principle: Controller and DPO identification
requirement_groups.requirement_summary: At the time personal data is obtained directly from the data subject, the controller must disclose its identity and contact details (and its representative's, where applicable), plus the DPO's contact details where applicable.

sub_obligations.legal_text: the identity and the contact details of the controller and, where applicable, of the controller's representative
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The privacy notice must identify the controller (and its representative, if any) with contact details.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy identify the controller and provide contact details, including any representative where applicable?

sub_obligations.legal_text: the contact details of the data protection officer, where applicable
sub_obligations.plain_summary: If the company has a Data Protection Officer, their contact details must be provided.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy provide DPO contact details, if a DPO is required or appointed?

assessment_rules.met_when: The policy satisfies ALL sub-obligations: controller (and representative, if any) identity/contact details are disclosed, and DPO contact details are disclosed where a DPO applies.
assessment_rules.partially_met_when: Controller details are disclosed but DPO contact information is missing despite a DPO being required/appointed, or vice versa.
assessment_rules.not_met_when: The policy does not identify the controller or provide any contact details.
assessment_rules.conflicting_when: The policy provides no means of contacting the controller at all.
assessment_rules.insufficient_evidence_when: It cannot be determined from the policy whether a DPO exists or what the controller's full contact details are.

requirement_groups.principle: Purpose, legal basis, recipients and transfers
requirement_groups.requirement_summary: The controller must disclose the purposes and legal basis of processing, any legitimate interests relied on, recipients or categories of recipients (if any), and details of any international transfers and their safeguards (where applicable).

sub_obligations.legal_text: the purposes of the processing for which the personal data are intended as well as the legal basis for the processing
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The notice must explain why the data is being processed and the legal basis relied on.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy state the purposes of processing and the legal basis for each purpose?

sub_obligations.legal_text: where the processing is based on point (f) of Article 6(1), the legitimate interests pursued by the controller or by a third party
sub_obligations.plain_summary: If relying on legitimate interests as the legal basis, those interests must be described.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Where legitimate interests is the stated legal basis, does the policy describe those specific interests?

sub_obligations.legal_text: the recipients or categories of recipients of the personal data, if any
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The notice must state who the data is shared with, or categories of recipients.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy disclose the recipients or categories of recipients of personal data, if any exist?

sub_obligations.legal_text: the fact that the controller intends to transfer personal data to a third country or international organisation and the existence or absence of an adequacy decision...reference to the appropriate or suitable safeguards and the means by which to obtain a copy of them
sub_obligations.plain_summary: If data is transferred outside the EU, the notice must disclose this along with the safeguards used and how to get a copy of them.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Where international transfers occur, does the policy disclose the transfer, the adequacy status, and the applicable safeguards with access instructions?

assessment_rules.met_when: The policy satisfies ALL applicable sub-obligations: purposes and legal basis are stated for every processing activity, legitimate interests are described where relied on, recipients are disclosed if any exist, and transfer details/safeguards are disclosed if transfers occur.
assessment_rules.partially_met_when: Purposes and legal basis are disclosed but one or more applicable conditional items (legitimate interests, recipients, or transfer safeguards) are missing despite being relevant.
assessment_rules.not_met_when: The policy does not state purposes or legal bases for processing at all.
assessment_rules.conflicting_when: The policy discloses international transfers without any adequacy decision or safeguard reference, or claims a legal basis inconsistent with stated processing activities.
assessment_rules.insufficient_evidence_when: The policy does not provide enough detail to determine whether legitimate interests, recipients, or transfers apply and, if so, whether they are properly disclosed.

requirement_groups.principle: Storage period and core rights
requirement_groups.requirement_summary: The controller must disclose the data retention period (or criteria for determining it) and the existence of the rights of access, rectification, erasure, restriction, objection, and data portability.

sub_obligations.legal_text: the period for which the personal data will be stored, or if that is not possible, the criteria used to determine that period
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The notice must state how long data is kept, or the criteria used to decide that.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy state a retention period or the criteria used to determine one?

sub_obligations.legal_text: the existence of the right to request from the controller access to and rectification or erasure of personal data or restriction of processing concerning the data subject or to object to processing as well as the right to data portability
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The notice must inform people of their rights to access, correct, delete, restrict, object to processing, and port their data.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy list the rights of access, rectification, erasure, restriction, objection, and data portability?

assessment_rules.met_when: The policy satisfies ALL sub-obligations: a retention period or its criteria is stated, and all listed rights (access, rectification, erasure, restriction, objection, portability) are described.
assessment_rules.partially_met_when: A retention period is disclosed but some rights are omitted from the list, or vice versa.
assessment_rules.not_met_when: The policy discloses neither a retention period/criteria nor the listed rights.
assessment_rules.conflicting_when: The policy states data is kept indefinitely with no criteria, or denies the existence of one or more of the listed rights.
assessment_rules.insufficient_evidence_when: The policy's retention or rights statements are too vague to assess (e.g., 'as long as necessary' with no criteria and no rights list).

requirement_groups.principle: Consent withdrawal and complaint rights
requirement_groups.requirement_summary: Where consent is the legal basis, the controller must disclose the right to withdraw consent at any time without affecting prior lawful processing, and must always disclose the right to lodge a complaint with a supervisory authority.
requirement_groups.applicability_condition: The consent-withdrawal sub-obligation applies only where processing is based on consent under Article 6(1)(a) or 9(2)(a).

sub_obligations.legal_text: where the processing is based on point (a) of Article 6(1) or point (a) of Article 9(2), the existence of the right to withdraw consent at any time, without affecting the lawfulness of processing based on consent before its withdrawal
sub_obligations.plain_summary: If consent is the legal basis, the notice must explain the right to withdraw consent at any time without affecting past lawful processing.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Where consent is a stated legal basis, does the policy explain the right to withdraw consent at any time?

sub_obligations.legal_text: the right to lodge a complaint with a supervisory authority
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The notice must inform people they can complain to a data protection supervisory authority.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy inform data subjects of their right to lodge a complaint with a supervisory authority?

assessment_rules.met_when: The policy always discloses the right to complain to a supervisory authority, AND, where consent is a legal basis used, discloses the right to withdraw it at any time.
assessment_rules.partially_met_when: The complaint right is disclosed but consent withdrawal is not addressed despite consent being a stated legal basis, or vice versa.
assessment_rules.not_met_when: The policy discloses neither the complaint right nor consent withdrawal where applicable.
assessment_rules.conflicting_when: The policy states consent cannot be withdrawn once given, or denies the right to complain to a supervisory authority.
assessment_rules.insufficient_evidence_when: It is unclear from the policy whether consent is used as a legal basis, making it impossible to assess the withdrawal disclosure.

requirement_groups.principle: Statutory/contractual necessity and automated decision-making
requirement_groups.requirement_summary: The controller must disclose whether providing personal data is a statutory or contractual requirement (and consequences of not providing it), and, where automated decision-making including profiling under Article 22(1)/(4) occurs, must disclose its existence, logic, and significance/consequences.
requirement_groups.applicability_condition: The automated decision-making sub-obligation applies only where the controller engages in solely automated decision-making, including profiling, that produces legal or similarly significant effects.

sub_obligations.legal_text: whether the provision of personal data is a statutory or contractual requirement, or a requirement necessary to enter into a contract, as well as whether the data subject is obliged to provide the personal data and of the possible consequences of failure to provide such data
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The notice must say if providing the data is legally or contractually required, and what happens if the person doesn't provide it.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy state whether providing personal data is mandatory (statutory/contractual) and describe the consequences of not providing it?

sub_obligations.legal_text: the existence of automated decision-making, including profiling, referred to in Article 22(1) and (4) and, at least in those cases, meaningful information about the logic involved, as well as the significance and the envisaged consequences of such processing for the data subject
sub_obligations.plain_summary: If automated decisions or profiling significantly affect the person, the notice must explain that this happens, how it works, and what it means for them.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Where automated decision-making/profiling with significant effects occurs, does the policy disclose its existence, the logic involved, and its significance/consequences?

assessment_rules.met_when: The policy discloses whether data provision is mandatory and the consequences of refusal, AND, where automated decision-making/profiling with significant effects is used, discloses its existence, logic, and significance/consequences.
assessment_rules.partially_met_when: Mandatory-provision disclosure is present but automated decision-making disclosure is missing despite such processing occurring, or vice versa.
assessment_rules.not_met_when: The policy addresses neither the mandatory-provision disclosure nor automated decision-making despite the latter being used.
assessment_rules.conflicting_when: The policy engages in significant automated decision-making but explicitly denies using any such processing.
assessment_rules.insufficient_evidence_when: It cannot be determined from the policy whether automated decision-making with significant effects is used.

requirement_groups.principle: Notice of further processing for a new purpose
requirement_groups.requirement_summary: Before processing personal data for a purpose other than that for which it was collected, the controller must give the data subject prior information on that new purpose and any relevant Article 13(2) information.
requirement_groups.applicability_condition: Applies only where the controller intends to further process the personal data for a purpose different from the one for which it was originally collected.

sub_obligations.legal_text: the controller shall provide the data subject prior to that further processing with information on that other purpose and with any relevant further information as referred to in paragraph 2
sub_obligations.plain_summary: Before using data for a new purpose, the company must tell the person about that new purpose and give any other relevant Article 13(2) details.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Where data is reused for a new purpose, does the policy commit to notifying the data subject beforehand, including relevant Article 13(2) information?

assessment_rules.met_when: Where further processing for a new purpose occurs, the policy commits to providing prior notice of the new purpose and relevant Article 13(2) information.
assessment_rules.partially_met_when: The policy addresses purpose changes generally but does not clearly commit to prior notice before the new processing begins.
assessment_rules.not_met_when: The policy allows repurposing of data with no notice obligation described.
assessment_rules.conflicting_when: The policy states data may be used for new purposes without any notification to the data subject.
assessment_rules.insufficient_evidence_when: The policy does not address whether or how data may be repurposed.

requirement_groups.principle: Exemption where the data subject already has the information
requirement_groups.requirement_summary: The Article 13(1)-(3) disclosure obligations do not apply where and to the extent the data subject already possesses the information.
requirement_groups.applicability_condition: This is an exception clause: it applies only where the data subject already has the relevant information, and modifies the applicability of groups 13.1.ab, 13.1.cdef, 13.2.ab, 13.2.cd, 13.2.ef, and 13.3.

sub_obligations.legal_text: Paragraphs 1, 2 and 3 shall not apply where and insofar as the data subject already has the information.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The company does not need to repeat information the person already has.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy acknowledge that disclosure obligations do not apply where the data subject already possesses the relevant information?

expected_evidence: Policy statement on repeat disclosures or exemptions

assessment_rules.met_when: This is a proviso, not an independent obligation to check; when the exemption's factual condition holds for a given processing activity, the corresponding Article 13 disclosure groups should be marked not applicable rather than assessed as Met/Not Met.
assessment_rules.partially_met_when: Not applicable — this group modifies applicability of other groups rather than being independently partially satisfied.
assessment_rules.not_met_when: Not applicable in the ordinary sense; only relevant if the policy incorrectly claims the exemption applies when the data subject does not already have the information.
assessment_rules.conflicting_when: The policy invokes this exemption to avoid providing required information despite no evidence the data subject already has it.
assessment_rules.insufficient_evidence_when: It cannot be determined from the policy whether or when this exemption is being relied upon.

article.title: Information to be provided where personal data have not been obtained from the data subject

requirement_groups.principle: Controller and DPO identification
requirement_groups.requirement_summary: Where personal data is not obtained directly from the data subject, the controller must disclose its identity and contact details (and its representative's, where applicable), plus the DPO's contact details where applicable.

sub_obligations.legal_text: the identity and the contact details of the controller and, where applicable, of the controller's representative
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The notice must identify the controller (and its representative, if any) with contact details.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy identify the controller and provide contact details, including any representative where applicable?

sub_obligations.legal_text: the contact details of the data protection officer, where applicable
sub_obligations.plain_summary: If the company has a DPO, their contact details must be provided.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy provide DPO contact details, if a DPO is required or appointed?

assessment_rules.met_when: The policy satisfies ALL sub-obligations: controller (and representative, if any) identity/contact details are disclosed, and DPO contact details are disclosed where a DPO applies.
assessment_rules.partially_met_when: Controller details are disclosed but DPO contact information is missing despite a DPO being required/appointed, or vice versa.
assessment_rules.not_met_when: The policy does not identify the controller or provide any contact details.
assessment_rules.conflicting_when: The policy provides no means of contacting the controller at all.
