requirement_groups.requirement_summary: Where proportionate to the processing activities, the controller's compliance measures must include implementing appropriate internal data protection policies.
requirement_groups.applicability_condition: Applies where implementing internal data protection policies is proportionate to the controller's processing activities.

sub_obligations.legal_text: the measures referred to in paragraph 1 shall include the implementation of appropriate data protection policies by the controller
sub_obligations.plain_summary: Where appropriate, the company should have internal data protection policies in place.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Where proportionate, does the policy indicate that internal data protection policies have been implemented?

expected_evidence: Reference to internal data protection policy/governance documents

assessment_rules.met_when: Where proportionate, the policy indicates internal data protection policies have been implemented.
assessment_rules.partially_met_when: General compliance commitments exist but no specific internal policy is referenced despite apparent proportionality.
assessment_rules.not_met_when: No internal data protection policy is referenced despite processing activities that would warrant one.
assessment_rules.conflicting_when: The policy states no internal data protection governance exists despite substantial processing activities.
assessment_rules.insufficient_evidence_when: It cannot be determined whether internal policy implementation would be proportionate to the controller's activities.

requirement_groups.principle: Codes of conduct and certification as compliance evidence
requirement_groups.requirement_summary: Adherence to approved codes of conduct or approved certification mechanisms may be used as an element to demonstrate compliance with controller obligations.
requirement_groups.applicability_condition: Applies only where the controller adheres to an approved code of conduct or certification mechanism.

sub_obligations.legal_text: Adherence to approved codes of conduct as referred to in Article 40 or approved certification mechanisms as referred to in Article 42 may be used as an element by which to demonstrate compliance with the obligations of the controller.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: Following an approved code of conduct or certification can help show the company complies with its obligations.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy reference adherence to any approved code of conduct or certification mechanism as evidence of compliance?

assessment_rules.met_when: Where the controller adheres to a code of conduct or certification, the policy references it as supporting evidence of compliance.
assessment_rules.partially_met_when: Adherence is mentioned without clarity on which approved code or certification is involved.
assessment_rules.not_met_when: This group is not applicable if no such adherence exists; not_met only applies if adherence is claimed without any substantiation.
assessment_rules.conflicting_when: The policy claims certification or code adherence that appears inconsistent with the rest of the policy's disclosures.
assessment_rules.insufficient_evidence_when: It cannot be determined whether the controller adheres to any approved code of conduct or certification mechanism.

article.title: Data protection by design and by default

requirement_groups.principle: Data protection by design
requirement_groups.requirement_summary: The controller must implement appropriate technical and organisational measures, such as pseudonymisation, at the time of determining processing means and at the time of processing, designed to effectively implement data protection principles and integrate necessary safeguards into the processing.

sub_obligations.legal_text: the controller shall...implement appropriate technical and organisational measures, such as pseudonymisation, which are designed to implement data-protection principles, such as data minimisation, in an effective manner and to integrate the necessary safeguards into the processing
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The company must build data protection into its systems from the start, using measures like pseudonymisation to apply principles like data minimisation effectively.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy describe measures such as pseudonymisation implemented at the design stage to embed data protection principles into processing?

assessment_rules.met_when: The policy describes technical/organisational measures implemented at the design stage to embed data protection principles into processing.
assessment_rules.partially_met_when: General privacy-by-design language is used without describing specific measures.
assessment_rules.not_met_when: The policy does not address privacy-by-design at all.
assessment_rules.conflicting_when: The policy states data protection is only considered after systems are built and deployed.
assessment_rules.insufficient_evidence_when: It cannot be determined whether design-stage privacy measures are implemented.

requirement_groups.principle: Data protection by default
requirement_groups.requirement_summary: By default, only personal data necessary for each specific purpose is processed, covering the amount collected, extent of processing, storage period, and accessibility, and by default personal data must not be made accessible without the individual's intervention to an indefinite number of people.

sub_obligations.legal_text: the controller shall implement appropriate technical and organisational measures for ensuring that, by default, only personal data which are necessary for each specific purpose of the processing are processed
sub_obligations.plain_summary: By default, systems should only process the minimum data needed for each purpose.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy describe default settings that limit data processing to what is necessary for each specific purpose?

sub_obligations.legal_text: That obligation applies to the amount of personal data collected, the extent of their processing, the period of their storage and their accessibility.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: This default-minimisation applies to how much data is collected, how it's used, how long it's kept, and who can access it.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy indicate that default minimisation applies across data collection amount, processing extent, storage period, and accessibility?

sub_obligations.legal_text: such measures shall ensure that by default personal data are not made accessible without the individual's intervention to an indefinite number of natural persons
sub_obligations.plain_summary: By default, personal data shouldn't be visible to an unlimited number of people unless the individual takes action to make it so.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy confirm that personal data is not, by default, accessible to an indefinite number of people without the individual's intervention?

assessment_rules.met_when: The policy satisfies ALL sub-obligations: default settings limit data to what is necessary across collection/processing/storage/accessibility, and data is not made broadly accessible by default without user action.
assessment_rules.partially_met_when: Some default-minimisation aspects are addressed but accessibility defaults are not, or vice versa.
assessment_rules.not_met_when: The policy does not describe any default privacy-protective settings.
assessment_rules.conflicting_when: The policy states data is made publicly accessible by default without user action.
assessment_rules.insufficient_evidence_when: The policy's default-settings description is too vague to assess minimisation across all four dimensions.

requirement_groups.principle: Certification as compliance evidence for design/default requirements
requirement_groups.requirement_summary: An approved certification mechanism may be used as an element to demonstrate compliance with the data protection by design and by default requirements.
requirement_groups.applicability_condition: Applies only where the controller holds an approved certification.

sub_obligations.legal_text: An approved certification mechanism pursuant to Article 42 may be used as an element to demonstrate compliance with the requirements set out in paragraphs 1 and 2 of this Article.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: Holding an approved certification can help show compliance with design/default requirements.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy reference an approved certification mechanism supporting compliance with design/default obligations, where applicable?

assessment_rules.met_when: Where held, an approved certification is referenced as supporting evidence for design/default compliance.
assessment_rules.partially_met_when: Certification is mentioned without specifying its relevance to design/default requirements.
assessment_rules.not_met_when: Not applicable in the ordinary case where no certification is held.
assessment_rules.conflicting_when: The policy claims a certification inconsistent with its other disclosures.
assessment_rules.insufficient_evidence_when: It cannot be determined whether the controller holds any approved certification.

requirement_groups.principle: Transparent allocation of joint controller responsibilities
requirement_groups.requirement_summary: Where two or more controllers jointly determine the purposes and means of processing, they must transparently determine their respective responsibilities, particularly for exercising data subject rights and Article 13/14 duties, via an arrangement, unless determined by law; the arrangement may designate a data subject contact point.
requirement_groups.applicability_condition: Applies only where the controller is a joint controller with one or more other controllers.

sub_obligations.legal_text: They shall in a transparent manner determine their respective responsibilities for compliance with the obligations under this Regulation, in particular as regards the exercising of the rights of the data subject and their respective duties to provide the information referred to in Articles 13 and 14, by means of an arrangement between them
sub_obligations.plain_summary: Joint controllers must clearly divide up who handles which GDPR obligations, especially rights requests and privacy notices, through a formal arrangement.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Where joint controllers exist, does the policy describe a transparent arrangement allocating responsibilities for data subject rights and Article 13/14 disclosures?

sub_obligations.legal_text: The arrangement may designate a contact point for data subjects.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The joint-controller arrangement can name a single contact point for data subjects to reach.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy indicate whether a contact point for data subjects has been designated under the joint-controller arrangement?

expected_evidence: Joint controller arrangement summary in the policy

assessment_rules.met_when: Where joint controllership exists, the policy satisfies ALL sub-obligations: a transparent responsibility allocation is described (or law-based allocation is noted), and whether a contact point exists is addressed.
assessment_rules.partially_met_when: Joint controllership is disclosed but responsibility allocation or the contact point question is not addressed.
assessment_rules.not_met_when: Joint controllership exists with no disclosure of any responsibility arrangement.
assessment_rules.conflicting_when: The policy discloses joint controllership but states no allocation of responsibilities has been made.
assessment_rules.insufficient_evidence_when: It cannot be determined whether the controller processes any data jointly with another controller.

requirement_groups.principle: Accuracy and availability of the joint-controller arrangement
requirement_groups.requirement_summary: The joint-controller arrangement must duly reflect the respective roles and relationships of the joint controllers vis-à-vis data subjects, and its essence must be made available to the data subject.
requirement_groups.applicability_condition: Applies only where joint controllership exists.

sub_obligations.legal_text: The arrangement referred to in paragraph 1 shall duly reflect the respective roles and relationships of the joint controllers vis-à-vis the data subjects.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The arrangement must accurately reflect how each joint controller actually relates to data subjects.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy indicate that the joint-controller arrangement accurately reflects each controller's role toward data subjects?

sub_obligations.legal_text: The essence of the arrangement shall be made available to the data subject.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: Data subjects must be able to see the key points of the joint-controller arrangement.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy make the essence of the joint-controller arrangement available to data subjects (e.g., in the privacy notice)?

expected_evidence: Summary of joint-controller roles published in the policy

assessment_rules.met_when: Where joint controllership exists, the policy satisfies ALL sub-obligations: it accurately reflects respective roles and makes the essence of the arrangement available to data subjects.
assessment_rules.partially_met_when: Roles are described but the arrangement's essence is not made available to data subjects, or vice versa.
assessment_rules.not_met_when: No disclosure of the arrangement or its essence is made to data subjects.
assessment_rules.conflicting_when: The policy describes roles inconsistent with the actual joint processing described elsewhere.
assessment_rules.insufficient_evidence_when: It cannot be determined whether the joint-controller arrangement's essence has been made available to data subjects.

requirement_groups.principle: Data subject rights against each joint controller
requirement_groups.requirement_summary: Irrespective of the arrangement's terms, the data subject may exercise their rights under the Regulation against each of the joint controllers.
requirement_groups.applicability_condition: Applies only where joint controllership exists.

sub_obligations.legal_text: Irrespective of the terms of the arrangement referred to in paragraph 1, the data subject may exercise his or her rights under this Regulation in respect of and against each of the controllers.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: No matter what the joint controllers agreed among themselves, the data subject can exercise their rights against any of them.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy confirm that data subjects may exercise their rights against any joint controller regardless of the internal arrangement?

expected_evidence: Statement confirming rights exercisable against any joint controller

assessment_rules.met_when: Where joint controllership exists, the policy confirms data subjects may exercise their rights against any joint controller regardless of internal allocation.
assessment_rules.partially_met_when: The internal allocation is described but it's unclear whether data subjects can still approach any controller directly.
assessment_rules.not_met_when: The policy suggests data subjects must only contact a designated party and cannot approach other controllers directly.
assessment_rules.conflicting_when: The policy states data subjects can only exercise rights against the contact point, contrary to the Regulation.
assessment_rules.insufficient_evidence_when: It cannot be determined how data subjects would exercise rights in a joint-controller scenario.

article.title: Representatives of controllers or processors not established in the Union

requirement_groups.principle: Obligation to designate an EU representative
requirement_groups.requirement_summary: Where Article 3(2) applies (non-EU controller/processor targeting or monitoring EU data subjects), the controller or processor must designate a representative in the Union in writing.
requirement_groups.applicability_condition: Applies only where Article 3(2) applies, i.e., a non-EU controller or processor offers goods/services to, or monitors the behaviour of, data subjects in the Union.

sub_obligations.legal_text: the controller or the processor shall designate in writing a representative in the Union
sub_obligations.plain_summary: Non-EU companies covered by GDPR must appoint an EU representative in writing.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Where the controller is established outside the EU but subject to GDPR, does the policy identify a written designation of an EU representative?

expected_evidence: EU representative identification and contact details

assessment_rules.met_when: Where applicable, the policy identifies a designated EU representative.
assessment_rules.partially_met_when: A representative is referenced without confirmation of written designation.
assessment_rules.not_met_when: No representative is identified despite Article 3(2) applying.
assessment_rules.conflicting_when: The policy states no representative will be designated despite Article 3(2) applying and no exemption being claimed.
assessment_rules.insufficient_evidence_when: It cannot be determined whether the controller is established outside the EU or whether Article 3(2) applies.

requirement_groups.principle: Exemptions from the representative requirement
requirement_groups.requirement_summary: The representative-designation obligation does not apply to occasional, low-risk processing not involving large-scale special category or criminal data, or to processing by a public authority or body.
requirement_groups.applicability_condition: Applies only where the controller claims exemption from designating an EU representative.

sub_obligations.legal_text: processing which is occasional, does not include, on a large scale, processing of special categories of data as referred to in Article 9(1) or processing of personal data relating to criminal convictions and offences referred to in Article 10, and is unlikely to result in a risk to the rights and freedoms of natural persons
sub_obligations.plain_summary: No representative is needed if processing is occasional, doesn't involve large-scale sensitive/criminal data, and poses low risk.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy justify a representative exemption based on occasional, low-risk, non-large-scale sensitive-data processing, where claimed?

sub_obligations.legal_text: a public authority or body
sub_obligations.plain_summary: Public authorities and bodies are exempt from the representative requirement.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy identify the controller as a public authority or body, where relied upon as an exemption?

assessment_rules.met_when: Where no representative is designated, the policy documents AT LEAST ONE valid exemption ground consistent with the facts.
assessment_rules.partially_met_when: An exemption is claimed but not clearly substantiated.
assessment_rules.not_met_when: No representative is designated and no exemption is claimed or justified.
assessment_rules.conflicting_when: The policy claims the occasional/low-risk exemption while describing large-scale or high-risk processing.
assessment_rules.insufficient_evidence_when: It cannot be determined whether the controller qualifies for either exemption.

requirement_groups.principle: Location and mandate of the representative
requirement_groups.requirement_summary: The representative must be established in a Member State where the relevant data subjects are located, and must be mandated to be addressed by supervisory authorities and data subjects on all processing-related compliance issues.
requirement_groups.applicability_condition: Applies only where a representative is designated under Article 27(1).

sub_obligations.legal_text: The representative shall be established in one of the Member States where the data subjects, whose personal data are processed in relation to the offering of goods or services to them, or whose behaviour is monitored, are.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The representative must be located in a Member State where the affected data subjects are.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy confirm the representative is established in a Member State where the relevant data subjects are located?

sub_obligations.legal_text: The representative shall be mandated by the controller or processor to be addressed in addition to or instead of the controller or the processor by, in particular, supervisory authorities and data subjects, on all issues related to processing
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The representative must be authorized to handle inquiries from supervisory authorities and data subjects on the company's behalf.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy confirm the representative is mandated to be addressed by supervisory authorities and data subjects on processing issues?

expected_evidence: Representative contact details and mandate description

assessment_rules.met_when: Where a representative is designated, the policy satisfies ALL sub-obligations: correct Member State establishment and a proper mandate to be addressed by authorities/data subjects.
assessment_rules.partially_met_when: The representative is named but the mandate scope or location basis is unclear.
assessment_rules.not_met_when: A representative is designated with no indication of proper location or mandate.
assessment_rules.conflicting_when: The representative is located outside any Member State where relevant data subjects are.
assessment_rules.insufficient_evidence_when: It cannot be determined where the representative is established or what they are mandated to do.

requirement_groups.principle: Representative designation does not shield the controller from legal action
requirement_groups.requirement_summary: Designating a representative does not prejudice legal actions that could be initiated against the controller or processor themselves.
requirement_groups.applicability_condition: Applies only where a representative is designated.

sub_obligations.legal_text: The designation of a representative by the controller or processor shall be without prejudice to legal actions which could be initiated against the controller or the processor themselves.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: Having a representative doesn't protect the company itself from being legally pursued directly.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy avoid suggesting that the representative shields the controller from direct legal liability?

expected_evidence: Statement clarifying representative's role does not limit controller liability

assessment_rules.met_when: The policy does not claim or imply that the representative shields the controller from direct legal action.
assessment_rules.partially_met_when: The policy does not address this point but also does not misstate it.
assessment_rules.not_met_when: Not typically assessable as 'not met' absent an explicit misstatement.
assessment_rules.conflicting_when: The policy states the representative bears sole legal responsibility instead of the controller.
assessment_rules.insufficient_evidence_when: The policy does not address the legal relationship between the representative and the controller's liability.

requirement_groups.principle: Use of processors offering sufficient guarantees
requirement_groups.requirement_summary: The controller must use only processors that provide sufficient guarantees to implement appropriate technical and organisational measures meeting GDPR requirements and protecting data subject rights.
requirement_groups.applicability_condition: Applies only where the controller engages a processor.

sub_obligations.legal_text: the controller shall use only processors providing sufficient guarantees to implement appropriate technical and organisational measures in such a manner that processing will meet the requirements of this Regulation and ensure the protection of the rights of the data subject
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The company can only work with processors that can demonstrate they will handle data securely and compliantly.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy describe a due-diligence process for selecting processors that provide sufficient GDPR compliance guarantees?

assessment_rules.met_when: Where processors are used, the policy describes a process for verifying processors provide sufficient compliance guarantees.
assessment_rules.partially_met_when: Processors are mentioned without any vetting process described.
assessment_rules.not_met_when: No due-diligence process is described despite the use of processors.
assessment_rules.conflicting_when: The policy states processors are engaged without any compliance vetting.
assessment_rules.insufficient_evidence_when: It cannot be determined whether the controller uses processors.

requirement_groups.principle: Sub-processor engagement authorization
requirement_groups.requirement_summary: A processor may not engage another processor without the controller's prior specific or general written authorisation; under general authorisation, the processor must inform the controller of intended sub-processor changes, giving the controller an opportunity to object.
requirement_groups.applicability_condition: Applies only where a processor intends to engage a sub-processor.

sub_obligations.legal_text: The processor shall not engage another processor without prior specific or general written authorisation of the controller.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: Processors need the controller's written permission before bringing in a sub-processor.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy confirm sub-processor engagement requires prior written authorisation from the controller?

sub_obligations.legal_text: In the case of general written authorisation, the processor shall inform the controller of any intended changes concerning the addition or replacement of other processors, thereby giving the controller the opportunity to object to such changes.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: If general permission was given, the processor must still notify the controller of any new or replaced sub-processors and allow objections.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Under general authorisation, does the policy confirm the controller is notified of sub-processor changes with an opportunity to object?

assessment_rules.met_when: The policy satisfies ALL sub-obligations: sub-processor engagement requires written authorisation, and under general authorisation, notice and objection rights are provided.
assessment_rules.partially_met_when: Authorisation is required but the notice/objection mechanism under general authorisation is not described.
assessment_rules.not_met_when: Sub-processors may be engaged without any authorisation process described.
assessment_rules.conflicting_when: The policy allows sub-processor engagement without controller authorisation of any kind.
assessment_rules.insufficient_evidence_when: It cannot be determined whether the controller's processors engage sub-processors.

requirement_groups.principle: Mandatory processor contract terms
requirement_groups.requirement_summary: Processing by a processor must be governed by a binding contract or legal act specifying the subject-matter, duration, nature, purpose, data types, categories of data subjects, and obligations/rights of the controller, and stipulating that the processor: acts only on documented instructions (with limited exceptions); ensures confidentiality commitments by authorised personnel; implements Article 32 security measures; respects sub-processor engagement conditions; assists with data subject rights requests; assists with Articles 32-36 compliance; deletes or returns data at the end of services; and makes information available for compliance demonstration and audits.
requirement_groups.applicability_condition: Applies only where processing is carried out on the controller's behalf by a processor.

sub_obligations.legal_text: processes the personal data only on documented instructions from the controller, including with regard to transfers of personal data to a third country or an international organisation, unless required to do so by Union or Member State law to which the processor is subject
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The processor must act only on the controller's documented instructions, including for international transfers, unless a law requires otherwise.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the contract or policy confirm the processor acts only on documented instructions from the controller?

sub_obligations.legal_text: ensures that persons authorised to process the personal data have committed themselves to confidentiality or are under an appropriate statutory obligation of confidentiality
sub_obligations.plain_summary: People processing the data for the processor must be bound by confidentiality.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the contract require processor personnel to be bound by confidentiality obligations?

sub_obligations.legal_text: takes all measures required pursuant to Article 32
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The processor must implement the required security measures.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the contract require the processor to implement Article 32 security measures?

sub_obligations.legal_text: respects the conditions referred to in paragraphs 2 and 4 for engaging another processor
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The processor must follow the rules for bringing in sub-processors.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the contract require the processor to respect sub-processor engagement conditions?

sub_obligations.legal_text: assists the controller by appropriate technical and organisational measures, insofar as this is possible, for the fulfilment of the controller's obligation to respond to requests for exercising the data subject's rights
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The processor must help the controller respond to data subject rights requests.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the contract require the processor to assist with fulfilling data subject rights requests?

sub_obligations.legal_text: assists the controller in ensuring compliance with the obligations pursuant to Articles 32 to 36
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The processor must help the controller comply with security, breach notification, and DPIA obligations.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the contract require the processor to assist with Articles 32-36 compliance?

sub_obligations.legal_text: at the choice of the controller, deletes or returns all the personal data to the controller after the end of the provision of services relating to processing, and deletes existing copies unless Union or Member State law requires storage of the personal data
sub_obligations.plain_summary: At the end of the engagement, the processor must delete or return all data as the controller chooses, and delete copies, unless law requires retention.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the contract require the processor to delete or return data (and delete copies) at the end of the engagement, unless law requires retention?

sub_obligations.legal_text: makes available to the controller all information necessary to demonstrate compliance with the obligations laid down in this Article and allow for and contribute to audits, including inspections, conducted by the controller or another auditor mandated by the controller
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The processor must provide information to demonstrate compliance and support audits by the controller.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the contract require the processor to provide compliance information and support audits/inspections?

assessment_rules.met_when: The policy or referenced contract satisfies ALL sub-obligations (a-h) governing the processor relationship.
assessment_rules.partially_met_when: The contract addresses some but not all of the required terms.
assessment_rules.not_met_when: No processor contract terms are described at all despite using processors.
assessment_rules.conflicting_when: The contract explicitly permits the processor to act outside documented instructions, retain data indefinitely without legal basis, or refuses audit cooperation.
assessment_rules.insufficient_evidence_when: It cannot be determined what terms govern the relationship between the controller and its processors.

requirement_groups.principle: Flow-down of obligations to sub-processors and processor liability
requirement_groups.requirement_summary: Where a processor engages a sub-processor, the same data protection obligations must be imposed on the sub-processor by contract, and the initial processor remains fully liable to the controller for the sub-processor's performance if it fails to meet its obligations.
requirement_groups.applicability_condition: Applies only where a processor engages a sub-processor.

sub_obligations.legal_text: the same data protection obligations as set out in the contract or other legal act between the controller and the processor...shall be imposed on that other processor by way of a contract or other legal act
sub_obligations.plain_summary: Sub-processors must be bound by the same data protection terms as the main processor.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Where sub-processors are used, does the contract confirm the same obligations are flowed down to them?

sub_obligations.legal_text: Where that other processor fails to fulfil its data protection obligations, the initial processor shall remain fully liable to the controller for the performance of that other processor's obligations.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: If the sub-processor fails to meet its obligations, the main processor remains fully responsible to the controller.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the contract confirm the initial processor remains fully liable for a sub-processor's failures?

assessment_rules.met_when: Where sub-processors are used, the policy/contract satisfies ALL sub-obligations: obligations flow down and the primary processor remains fully liable.
assessment_rules.partially_met_when: Flow-down obligations are described but liability allocation is not, or vice versa.
assessment_rules.not_met_when: No flow-down or liability provisions are described despite sub-processor use.
assessment_rules.conflicting_when: The contract releases the primary processor from liability for sub-processor failures.
assessment_rules.insufficient_evidence_when: It cannot be determined whether sub-processors are used or how obligations/liability are structured.

requirement_groups.principle: Certification and standard contractual clauses as compliance tools
requirement_groups.requirement_summary: Processor adherence to an approved code of conduct or certification may evidence sufficient guarantees, and the controller-processor contract may be based on standard contractual clauses issued by the Commission or a supervisory authority.
requirement_groups.applicability_condition: Applies only where the controller/processor relies on codes of conduct, certification, or standard contractual clauses for their arrangement.

sub_obligations.legal_text: Adherence of a processor to an approved code of conduct...or an approved certification mechanism...may be used as an element by which to demonstrate sufficient guarantees
sub_obligations.plain_summary: A processor's certification or code adherence can help show it offers sufficient guarantees.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy reference processor certification or code-of-conduct adherence as evidence of sufficient guarantees, where applicable?

sub_obligations.legal_text: the contract or the other legal act...may be based, in whole or in part, on standard contractual clauses
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The processor contract can be based on official standard contractual clauses.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy indicate the processor contract is based on standard contractual clauses, where applicable?

expected_evidence: Reference to SCCs or certification in processor agreements

assessment_rules.met_when: Where relied upon, the policy documents AT LEAST ONE of certification/code adherence or use of standard contractual clauses.
assessment_rules.partially_met_when: A tool is referenced without clarity on its scope or applicability.
assessment_rules.not_met_when: Not applicable in the ordinary case; only relevant if these tools are claimed without substantiation.
assessment_rules.conflicting_when: The policy claims SCC use inconsistent with the described data flows.
assessment_rules.insufficient_evidence_when: It cannot be determined whether the controller relies on these tools for its processor arrangements.

requirement_groups.principle: Written form of processor contracts and processor liability as controller
requirement_groups.requirement_summary: The processor contract or legal act must be in writing, including electronic form, and a processor that determines the purposes and means of processing in violation of the Regulation is considered a controller for that processing.

sub_obligations.legal_text: The contract or the other legal act referred to in paragraphs 3 and 4 shall be in writing, including in electronic form.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: Processor contracts must be documented in writing, which can be electronic.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy confirm processor contracts are documented in writing, including electronic form?

sub_obligations.legal_text: if a processor infringes this Regulation by determining the purposes and means of processing, the processor shall be considered to be a controller in respect of that processing
sub_obligations.plain_summary: If a processor oversteps and decides why/how data is processed, it becomes legally treated as a controller for that processing.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy acknowledge that a processor exceeding its role by determining purposes and means becomes a controller for that processing?

assessment_rules.met_when: The policy satisfies ALL sub-obligations: processor contracts are confirmed to be in writing/electronic form, and the processor-becomes-controller consequence is acknowledged where relevant.
assessment_rules.partially_met_when: Written form is confirmed but the processor-liability consequence is not addressed.
assessment_rules.not_met_when: Neither element is addressed despite the use of processors.
assessment_rules.conflicting_when: The policy states processor arrangements are informal/undocumented.
assessment_rules.insufficient_evidence_when: It cannot be determined how processor contracts are documented.

article.title: Processing under the authority of the controller or processor

requirement_groups.principle: Instruction-based processing by persons under authority
requirement_groups.requirement_summary: The processor and any person acting under the controller's or processor's authority who has access to personal data must not process it except on the controller's instructions, unless required to do so by law.

sub_obligations.legal_text: The processor and any person acting under the authority of the controller or of the processor, who has access to personal data, shall not process those data except on instructions from the controller, unless required to do so by Union or Member State law.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: Anyone with access to the data through the processor or controller can only act on the controller's instructions, unless a law requires otherwise.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy confirm that personnel and processors with data access act only on the controller's instructions, absent a legal requirement otherwise?

assessment_rules.met_when: The policy confirms that all persons with data access, whether processor staff or controller personnel, act only on the controller's instructions unless legally required otherwise.
assessment_rules.partially_met_when: Instruction-based processing is stated for the processor but not for other personnel under the controller's authority, or vice versa.
assessment_rules.not_met_when: The policy does not address instruction-based limitations on data processing.
assessment_rules.conflicting_when: The policy allows personnel or processors to process data outside instructions without any legal basis.
assessment_rules.insufficient_evidence_when: The policy does not describe how access to data by personnel or processors is controlled.

requirement_groups.principle: Controller's record of processing activities content
requirement_groups.requirement_summary: Each controller (and representative, where applicable) must maintain a record of processing activities containing: controller/DPO contact details, purposes of processing, categories of data subjects and personal data, categories of recipients, international transfer details with safeguards, envisaged erasure time limits, and a general description of security measures.
requirement_groups.applicability_condition: Subject to the small-enterprise exemption in group 30.5.

sub_obligations.legal_text: the name and contact details of the controller and, where applicable, the joint controller, the controller's representative and the data protection officer
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The record must identify the controller, joint controllers, representative, and DPO with contact details.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the record of processing activities include controller, joint controller, representative, and DPO contact details?

sub_obligations.legal_text: the purposes of the processing
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The record must list the purposes of each processing activity.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the record include the purposes of each processing activity?

sub_obligations.legal_text: a description of the categories of data subjects and of the categories of personal data
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The record must describe the types of people and data involved.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the record describe the categories of data subjects and personal data?

sub_obligations.legal_text: the categories of recipients to whom the personal data have been or will be disclosed including recipients in third countries or international organisations
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The record must list categories of recipients, including any abroad.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the record include categories of recipients, including any in third countries or international organisations?

sub_obligations.legal_text: where applicable, transfers of personal data to a third country or an international organisation, including the identification of that third country or international organisation and...the documentation of suitable safeguards
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The record must document any international transfers and the safeguards used.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Where transfers occur, does the record identify the destination country/organisation and document the safeguards used?

sub_obligations.legal_text: where possible, the envisaged time limits for erasure of the different categories of data
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The record should include planned erasure timeframes for data categories, where possible.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the record include envisaged erasure time limits for different data categories, where possible?

sub_obligations.legal_text: where possible, a general description of the technical and organisational security measures referred to in Article 32(1)
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The record should include a general description of the security measures used, where possible.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the record include a general description of the technical and organisational security measures applied?

assessment_rules.met_when: The controller maintains a record satisfying ALL applicable sub-obligations (a-g).
assessment_rules.partially_met_when: A record exists but omits one or more required elements.
assessment_rules.not_met_when: No record of processing activities is maintained despite the exemption not applying.
assessment_rules.conflicting_when: The policy states no records are kept regardless of processing scale or risk.
assessment_rules.insufficient_evidence_when: It cannot be determined whether a record of processing activities is maintained or what it contains.

requirement_groups.principle: Processor's record of processing activities content
requirement_groups.requirement_summary: Each processor (and representative, where applicable) must maintain a record of all categories of processing carried out on behalf of controllers, containing processor/controller/DPO contact details, categories of processing, international transfer details with safeguards, and a general description of security measures.
requirement_groups.applicability_condition: Applies only where the entity acts as a processor. Subject to the small-enterprise exemption in group 30.5.

sub_obligations.legal_text: the name and contact details of the processor or processors and of each controller on behalf of which the processor is acting, and, where applicable, of the controller's or the processor's representative, and the data protection officer
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The processor's record must identify the processor(s), each controller it acts for, any representatives, and the DPO.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the processor's record include contact details for the processor, each controller, representatives, and the DPO?

sub_obligations.legal_text: the categories of processing carried out on behalf of each controller
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The record must describe categories of processing done for each controller.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the processor's record describe the categories of processing carried out for each controller?

sub_obligations.legal_text: where applicable, transfers of personal data to a third country or an international organisation, including the identification of that third country or international organisation and...the documentation of suitable safeguards
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The record must document any international transfers and safeguards.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Where transfers occur, does the processor's record identify the destination and document safeguards?

sub_obligations.legal_text: where possible, a general description of the technical and organisational security measures referred to in Article 32(1)
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The record should generally describe the security measures used, where possible.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the processor's record include a general description of security measures, where possible?

assessment_rules.met_when: Where the entity acts as a processor, its record satisfies ALL applicable sub-obligations (a-d).
assessment_rules.partially_met_when: A processor record exists but omits one or more required elements.
assessment_rules.not_met_when: No processor record is maintained despite the exemption not applying.
assessment_rules.conflicting_when: The policy states no processor-side records are kept regardless of scale.
assessment_rules.insufficient_evidence_when: It cannot be determined whether the entity acts as a processor or maintains a processor record.

requirement_groups.principle: Form and availability of records
requirement_groups.requirement_summary: The records must be in writing, including electronic form, and made available to the supervisory authority on request.
requirement_groups.applicability_condition: Subject to the small-enterprise exemption in group 30.5.

sub_obligations.legal_text: The records referred to in paragraphs 1 and 2 shall be in writing, including in electronic form.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: Records must be documented in writing, which can be electronic.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy confirm records of processing activities are maintained in writing, including electronic form?

sub_obligations.legal_text: The controller or the processor and, where applicable, the controller's or the processor's representative, shall make the record available to the supervisory authority on request.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: Records must be made available to a supervisory authority if requested.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy confirm records will be made available to the supervisory authority on request?

assessment_rules.met_when: The policy satisfies ALL sub-obligations: records are maintained in writing/electronic form and made available to supervisory authorities on request.
assessment_rules.partially_met_when: Written record-keeping is confirmed but availability to supervisory authorities is not addressed, or vice versa.
assessment_rules.not_met_when: Neither element is addressed despite records being required.
assessment_rules.conflicting_when: The policy states records will not be disclosed to supervisory authorities upon request.
assessment_rules.insufficient_evidence_when: It cannot be determined how records are documented or whether they would be disclosed on request.

requirement_groups.principle: Small enterprise exemption from record-keeping
requirement_groups.requirement_summary: The record-keeping obligations do not apply to enterprises/organisations with fewer than 250 employees, unless the processing is likely to result in risk to data subjects, is not occasional, or includes special category or criminal conviction/offence data.
requirement_groups.applicability_condition: This is an exception clause: applies only where the controller/processor has fewer than 250 employees. If the controller meets this threshold but any of the three carve-out conditions (risk, non-occasional processing, or special category/criminal data) applies, the exemption does not apply and groups 30.1-30.4 should be assessed normally rather than marked not applicable.

sub_obligations.legal_text: The obligations referred to in paragraphs 1 and 2 shall not apply to an enterprise or an organisation employing fewer than 250 persons unless the processing it carries out is likely to result in a risk to the rights and freedoms of data subjects, the processing is not occasional, or the processing includes special categories of data...or personal data relating to criminal convictions and offences
sub_obligations.plain_summary: Small organizations under 250 employees don't need to keep formal processing records, unless their processing is risky, regular, or involves sensitive/criminal data.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Where the exemption is claimed, does the policy confirm the organisation has fewer than 250 employees and that none of the three carve-out conditions apply?

expected_evidence: Organisation size and exemption applicability statement

assessment_rules.met_when: Where the exemption is claimed, the policy confirms the organisation qualifies (under 250 employees, and no risk/non-occasional/special-category carve-out applies) — in which case groups 30.1-30.4 should be treated as not applicable rather than assessed.
assessment_rules.partially_met_when: The exemption is claimed without clarity on whether any carve-out condition applies.
assessment_rules.not_met_when: The exemption is claimed despite the organisation clearly meeting a carve-out condition (e.g., processing special category data regularly).
assessment_rules.conflicting_when: The policy claims the exemption while describing high-risk or special category data processing.
assessment_rules.insufficient_evidence_when: It cannot be determined whether the organisation qualifies for the small-enterprise exemption.

requirement_groups.principle: Duty to cooperate with the supervisory authority
requirement_groups.requirement_summary: The controller and processor (and their representatives, where applicable) must cooperate, on request, with the supervisory authority in the performance of its tasks.

sub_obligations.legal_text: The controller and the processor and, where applicable, their representatives, shall cooperate, on request, with the supervisory authority in the performance of its tasks.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The company must cooperate with data protection regulators when asked.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy commit to cooperating with the supervisory authority upon request?

assessment_rules.met_when: The policy confirms a commitment to cooperate with the supervisory authority upon request.
assessment_rules.partially_met_when: General regulatory compliance is mentioned without a specific cooperation commitment.
assessment_rules.not_met_when: The policy does not address cooperation with supervisory authorities at all.
assessment_rules.conflicting_when: The policy states it will not cooperate with regulatory requests.
assessment_rules.insufficient_evidence_when: The policy is silent on the topic of supervisory authority interactions.

requirement_groups.principle: Risk-appropriate technical and organisational security measures
requirement_groups.requirement_summary: The controller and processor must implement appropriate technical and organisational measures appropriate to the risk, including as appropriate: pseudonymisation and encryption; ability to ensure ongoing confidentiality, integrity, availability, and resilience of systems; ability to restore availability and access in a timely manner after an incident; and a process for regularly testing and evaluating the effectiveness of measures.

sub_obligations.legal_text: the pseudonymisation and encryption of personal data
sub_obligations.plain_summary: Data should be pseudonymised and encrypted where appropriate.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy describe the use of pseudonymisation and/or encryption as security measures, where appropriate?

sub_obligations.legal_text: the ability to ensure the ongoing confidentiality, integrity, availability and resilience of processing systems and services
sub_obligations.plain_summary: Systems must be kept confidential, accurate, available, and resilient on an ongoing basis.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy describe measures ensuring ongoing confidentiality, integrity, availability, and resilience of systems?

sub_obligations.legal_text: the ability to restore the availability and access to personal data in a timely manner in the event of a physical or technical incident
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The company must be able to restore data access quickly after an incident.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy describe a data recovery/restoration capability following incidents?

sub_obligations.legal_text: a process for regularly testing, assessing and evaluating the effectiveness of technical and organisational measures for ensuring the security of the processing
sub_obligations.plain_summary: Security measures must be regularly tested and evaluated for effectiveness.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy describe a process for regularly testing and evaluating the effectiveness of security measures?

assessment_rules.met_when: The policy satisfies ALL applicable sub-obligations: appropriate measures across encryption/pseudonymisation, confidentiality/integrity/availability/resilience, incident recovery, and regular testing.
assessment_rules.partially_met_when: Some security measures are described but not all four categories are addressed.
assessment_rules.not_met_when: The policy does not describe any technical or organisational security measures.
assessment_rules.conflicting_when: The policy states no security testing or recovery capability exists.
assessment_rules.insufficient_evidence_when: The policy's security statements are too generic to assess coverage of the four required categories.

requirement_groups.principle: Risk assessment factors for security measures
requirement_groups.requirement_summary: In assessing the appropriate level of security, account must be taken of risks presented by processing, particularly accidental or unlawful destruction, loss, alteration, unauthorised disclosure of, or access to, personal data.

sub_obligations.legal_text: In assessing the appropriate level of security account shall be taken in particular of the risks that are presented by processing, in particular from accidental or unlawful destruction, loss, alteration, unauthorised disclosure of, or access to personal data
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The security level chosen should reflect the actual risks of data loss, alteration, or unauthorized access/disclosure.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy indicate that security measures are chosen based on an assessment of risks like accidental/unlawful loss, alteration, or unauthorised access/disclosure?

assessment_rules.met_when: The policy indicates that security measures are informed by an assessment of processing-specific risks (loss, alteration, unauthorised access/disclosure).
assessment_rules.partially_met_when: Security measures are described without reference to any underlying risk assessment.
assessment_rules.not_met_when: No risk assessment process is described at all.
assessment_rules.conflicting_when: The policy states security measures are applied uniformly without regard to risk level.
assessment_rules.insufficient_evidence_when: It cannot be determined whether a risk assessment informs the security measures chosen.

requirement_groups.principle: Certification as security compliance evidence
requirement_groups.requirement_summary: Adherence to an approved code of conduct or certification mechanism may be used as an element to demonstrate compliance with the security requirements.
requirement_groups.applicability_condition: Applies only where the controller/processor holds an approved certification or code adherence.

sub_obligations.legal_text: Adherence to an approved code of conduct as referred to in Article 40 or an approved certification mechanism as referred to in Article 42 may be used as an element by which to demonstrate compliance with the requirements set out in paragraph 1 of this Article.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: Holding an approved certification or code adherence can help show the company meets security requirements.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy reference an approved certification or code of conduct as evidence of security compliance, where applicable?

assessment_rules.met_when: Where held, a certification or code adherence is referenced as supporting evidence of security compliance.
assessment_rules.partially_met_when: Certification is mentioned without specifying relevance to security requirements.
assessment_rules.not_met_when: Not applicable in the ordinary case where no certification is held.
assessment_rules.conflicting_when: The policy claims a security certification inconsistent with described practices.
assessment_rules.insufficient_evidence_when: It cannot be determined whether any security certification is held.

requirement_groups.principle: Instruction-based access control
requirement_groups.requirement_summary: The controller and processor must ensure that any natural person under their authority with access to personal data processes it only on instructions from the controller, unless required to do so by law.

sub_obligations.legal_text: The controller and processor shall take steps to ensure that any natural person acting under the authority of the controller or the processor who has access to personal data does not process them except on instructions from the controller, unless he or she is required to do so by Union or Member State law.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The company must ensure anyone with data access follows instructions, unless a law requires otherwise.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy describe access control measures ensuring personnel process data only on instructions unless legally required otherwise?

expected_evidence: Access control and personnel policy statements

assessment_rules.met_when: The policy describes steps ensuring personnel with data access act only on instructions, absent legal requirement otherwise.
assessment_rules.partially_met_when: General access control is mentioned without addressing the instruction-based limitation.
assessment_rules.not_met_when: No access control measures are described at all.
assessment_rules.conflicting_when: The policy allows personnel with data access to act outside instructions without legal basis.
assessment_rules.insufficient_evidence_when: The policy does not describe access controls for personnel with data access.

article.title: Notification of a personal data breach to the supervisory authority

requirement_groups.principle: Timely breach notification to the supervisory authority
requirement_groups.requirement_summary: The controller must notify a personal data breach to the competent supervisory authority without undue delay, and where feasible within 72 hours of becoming aware, unless the breach is unlikely to result in a risk to data subjects; late notifications must include reasons for the delay.
requirement_groups.applicability_condition: Applies whenever a personal data breach occurs that is not unlikely to result in a risk to data subjects.

sub_obligations.legal_text: the controller shall without undue delay and, where feasible, not later than 72 hours after having become aware of it, notify the personal data breach to the supervisory authority competent...unless the personal data breach is unlikely to result in a risk to the rights and freedoms of natural persons
sub_obligations.plain_summary: Breaches must generally be reported to the regulator within 72 hours of discovery, unless the breach poses no real risk.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy commit to notifying the supervisory authority of breaches without undue delay, and within 72 hours where feasible, unless the breach poses no risk?

sub_obligations.legal_text: Where the notification to the supervisory authority is not made within 72 hours, it shall be accompanied by reasons for the delay.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: If notification takes longer than 72 hours, the reasons for the delay must be explained.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy commit to explaining reasons for delay when notification exceeds 72 hours?

assessment_rules.met_when: The policy satisfies ALL sub-obligations: it commits to the 72-hour notification standard (with the no-risk exception) and to explaining delays beyond 72 hours.
assessment_rules.partially_met_when: A notification commitment exists but the delay-justification requirement is not addressed.
assessment_rules.not_met_when: No breach notification process is described at all.
assessment_rules.conflicting_when: The policy states breaches will not be reported to supervisory authorities regardless of risk.
assessment_rules.insufficient_evidence_when: The policy's breach notification statements are too vague to assess timing or delay-handling.

requirement_groups.principle: Processor notification to controller
requirement_groups.requirement_summary: The processor must notify the controller without undue delay after becoming aware of a personal data breach.
requirement_groups.applicability_condition: Applies only where the entity acts as a processor.

sub_obligations.legal_text: The processor shall notify the controller without undue delay after becoming aware of a personal data breach.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: Processors must alert the controller promptly upon discovering a breach.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Where the entity acts as a processor, does the policy/contract commit to notifying the controller without undue delay upon breach discovery?

assessment_rules.met_when: Where the entity is a processor, the policy commits to notifying the controller without undue delay upon breach discovery.
assessment_rules.partially_met_when: A breach notification process exists but timing commitments are vague.
assessment_rules.not_met_when: No processor-to-controller notification process is described.
assessment_rules.conflicting_when: The policy states breaches are not reported to the controller.
assessment_rules.insufficient_evidence_when: It cannot be determined whether the entity acts as a processor.

requirement_groups.principle: Content of breach notification to the supervisory authority
requirement_groups.requirement_summary: The notification must at least describe the nature of the breach (including categories/approximate numbers of data subjects and records), provide DPO or other contact details, describe likely consequences, and describe measures taken or proposed to address and mitigate the breach.
requirement_groups.applicability_condition: Applies where a breach notification to the supervisory authority is required.

sub_obligations.legal_text: describe the nature of the personal data breach including where possible, the categories and approximate number of data subjects concerned and the categories and approximate number of personal data records concerned
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The notification must describe what happened and, if possible, how many people/records were affected.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the notification content commitment include describing the nature and approximate scale of the breach?

sub_obligations.legal_text: communicate the name and contact details of the data protection officer or other contact point where more information can be obtained
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The notification must include a contact for more information.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the notification content commitment include DPO or other contact details?

sub_obligations.legal_text: describe the likely consequences of the personal data breach
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The notification must describe likely consequences of the breach.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the notification content commitment include a description of likely consequences?

sub_obligations.legal_text: describe the measures taken or proposed to be taken by the controller to address the personal data breach, including, where appropriate, measures to mitigate its possible adverse effects
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The notification must describe steps taken or planned to address and mitigate the breach.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the notification content commitment include measures taken/proposed to address and mitigate the breach?

assessment_rules.met_when: The policy commits to including ALL required content elements (a-d) in breach notifications to the supervisory authority.
assessment_rules.partially_met_when: Some but not all content elements are addressed.
assessment_rules.not_met_when: No content requirements are described for breach notifications.
assessment_rules.conflicting_when: The policy states notifications will omit required content such as mitigation measures.
assessment_rules.insufficient_evidence_when: It cannot be determined what content the breach notification would contain.

requirement_groups.principle: Phased provision of breach information
requirement_groups.requirement_summary: Where it is not possible to provide all required information simultaneously, it may be provided in phases without undue further delay.
requirement_groups.applicability_condition: Applies where not all required breach information is available at the time of initial notification.

sub_obligations.legal_text: Where, and in so far as, it is not possible to provide the information at the same time, the information may be provided in phases without undue further delay.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: If not all details are available right away, they can be provided later in stages, without unnecessary further delay.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy acknowledge that breach information may be provided in phases if not immediately available?

assessment_rules.met_when: The policy acknowledges that breach information may be phased in when not immediately available, provided without undue further delay.
assessment_rules.partially_met_when: Phasing is not explicitly addressed but the general notification commitment is otherwise sound.
assessment_rules.not_met_when: The policy insists on complete information before any notification occurs, contrary to the phased approach.
assessment_rules.conflicting_when: The policy states notification will be delayed indefinitely until all details are known.
assessment_rules.insufficient_evidence_when: The policy does not address how incomplete breach information is handled.

requirement_groups.principle: Documentation of personal data breaches
requirement_groups.requirement_summary: The controller must document any personal data breaches, comprising the facts, effects, and remedial action taken, enabling the supervisory authority to verify compliance.

sub_obligations.legal_text: The controller shall document any personal data breaches, comprising the facts relating to the personal data breach, its effects and the remedial action taken.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The company must keep records of all breaches, including what happened, the impact, and how it was addressed.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy commit to documenting all personal data breaches, including facts, effects, and remedial action?

sub_obligations.legal_text: That documentation shall enable the supervisory authority to verify compliance with this Article.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: This documentation must be detailed enough for regulators to check compliance.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy indicate the breach documentation is maintained in a way that would enable regulatory verification of compliance?

assessment_rules.met_when: The policy satisfies ALL sub-obligations: all breaches are documented with facts/effects/remedial action, sufficient for regulatory verification.
assessment_rules.partially_met_when: Breach documentation is described generically without confirming it would support regulatory verification.
assessment_rules.not_met_when: No breach documentation process is described.
assessment_rules.conflicting_when: The policy states breaches are not documented unless reported externally.
assessment_rules.insufficient_evidence_when: It cannot be determined whether or how breaches are documented internally.

article.title: Communication of a personal data breach to the data subject

requirement_groups.principle: Timely, clear communication of high-risk breaches to data subjects
requirement_groups.requirement_summary: Where a breach is likely to result in a high risk to data subjects, the controller must communicate it to them without undue delay, in clear and plain language, describing the breach's nature and containing at least the DPO/contact details, likely consequences, and measures taken/proposed to address and mitigate it.
requirement_groups.applicability_condition: Applies where a personal data breach is likely to result in a high risk to the rights and freedoms of data subjects, and none of the exemptions in group 34.3 apply.

sub_obligations.legal_text: When the personal data breach is likely to result in a high risk to the rights and freedoms of natural persons, the controller shall communicate the personal data breach to the data subject without undue delay.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: High-risk breaches must be communicated to affected individuals promptly.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy commit to communicating high-risk breaches to affected individuals without undue delay?

sub_obligations.legal_text: The communication to the data subject...shall describe in clear and plain language the nature of the personal data breach and contain at least the information and measures referred to in points (b), (c) and (d) of Article 33(3).
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The communication to individuals must be in plain language and include contact details, likely consequences, and mitigation measures.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy commit to communicating breaches in clear, plain language including contact details, consequences, and mitigation measures?

assessment_rules.met_when: Where a high-risk breach occurs and no exemption applies, the policy satisfies ALL sub-obligations: prompt communication in plain language with the required content.
assessment_rules.partially_met_when: A communication commitment exists but plain-language or content requirements are not addressed.
assessment_rules.not_met_when: No process is described for communicating high-risk breaches to data subjects.
assessment_rules.conflicting_when: The policy states data subjects will not be informed of high-risk breaches under any circumstances.
assessment_rules.insufficient_evidence_when: The policy's breach communication statements are too vague to assess timing, language, or content.

requirement_groups.principle: Exemptions from data subject breach communication
requirement_groups.requirement_summary: Communication to the data subject is not required where the controller has implemented protective measures (e.g., encryption) rendering the data unintelligible, has taken subsequent measures ensuring the high risk no longer materialises, or where communication would involve disproportionate effort — in which case a public communication or similarly effective measure must be used instead.
requirement_groups.applicability_condition: Applies only where the controller relies on an exemption from individually notifying data subjects of a high-risk breach.

sub_obligations.legal_text: the controller has implemented appropriate technical and organisational protection measures, and those measures were applied to the personal data affected by the personal data breach, in particular those that render the personal data unintelligible to any person who is not authorised to access it, such as encryption
sub_obligations.plain_summary: No individual notice is needed if protective measures like encryption made the breached data unreadable to unauthorized people.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Where this exemption is relied on, does the policy confirm protective measures such as encryption rendered the affected data unintelligible?

sub_obligations.legal_text: the controller has taken subsequent measures which ensure that the high risk to the rights and freedoms of data subjects referred to in paragraph 1 is no longer likely to materialise
sub_obligations.plain_summary: No individual notice is needed if follow-up actions have eliminated the high risk.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Where this exemption is relied on, does the policy describe subsequent measures that eliminated the high risk?

sub_obligations.legal_text: it would involve disproportionate effort. In such a case, there shall instead be a public communication or similar measure whereby the data subjects are informed in an equally effective manner.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: If individual notice would be disproportionately burdensome, a public communication of similar effectiveness must be used instead.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Where this exemption is relied on, does the policy describe an equally effective public communication used in place of individual notice?

assessment_rules.met_when: Where individual notice is not given, the policy documents AT LEAST ONE valid exemption ground, and for the disproportionate-effort ground, describes an equally effective public communication.
assessment_rules.partially_met_when: An exemption is invoked but the disproportionate-effort ground lacks a described alternative public communication.
assessment_rules.not_met_when: Individual notice is withheld with no exemption ground identified.
assessment_rules.conflicting_when: The policy invokes an exemption inconsistent with the facts (e.g., claims encryption rendered data unintelligible while describing plaintext storage).
assessment_rules.insufficient_evidence_when: It cannot be determined which exemption ground, if any, the controller relies on for a given breach.

requirement_groups.principle: Supervisory authority power to require communication
requirement_groups.requirement_summary: If the controller has not already communicated a breach to data subjects, the supervisory authority may require it to do so, or may determine that an exemption applies, after considering the likelihood of high risk.
requirement_groups.applicability_condition: Applies where the supervisory authority reviews a breach for which individual notice was not given.

sub_obligations.legal_text: If the controller has not already communicated the personal data breach to the data subject, the supervisory authority, having considered the likelihood of the personal data breach resulting in a high risk, may require it to do so or may decide that any of the conditions referred to in paragraph 3 are met.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: If the company hasn't told affected individuals about a breach, the regulator can step in and require it, or confirm an exemption applies.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy acknowledge that the supervisory authority may require individual breach notification even where the controller believed an exemption applied?

expected_evidence: Statement acknowledging supervisory authority oversight of breach notification decisions

assessment_rules.met_when: The policy acknowledges the supervisory authority's power to require individual notification or confirm an exemption.
assessment_rules.partially_met_when: The policy addresses exemptions but does not acknowledge supervisory authority oversight.
assessment_rules.not_met_when: The policy claims the controller has final say on notification decisions with no regulatory oversight.
assessment_rules.conflicting_when: The policy states it will not comply with a supervisory authority directive to notify.
assessment_rules.insufficient_evidence_when: The policy does not address the supervisory authority's role in breach notification decisions.

requirement_groups.principle: Requirement to carry out a DPIA
requirement_groups.requirement_summary: Where processing is likely to result in a high risk to data subjects, the controller must carry out a DPIA prior to processing; a DPIA is specifically required for systematic/extensive automated evaluation with legal/significant effects, large-scale special category or criminal data processing, or large-scale systematic monitoring of publicly accessible areas.
requirement_groups.applicability_condition: Applies where the controller undertakes a type of processing likely to result in high risk, including at least one of the three specifically listed high-risk processing types.

sub_obligations.legal_text: Where a type of processing...is likely to result in a high risk to the rights and freedoms of natural persons, the controller shall, prior to the processing, carry out an assessment of the impact of the envisaged processing operations on the protection of personal data.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: Before starting high-risk processing, the company must assess its data protection impact.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Where high-risk processing is undertaken, does the policy confirm a DPIA is carried out prior to that processing?
