sub_obligations.legal_text: a systematic and extensive evaluation of personal aspects relating to natural persons which is based on automated processing, including profiling, and on which decisions are based that produce legal effects...or similarly significantly affect the natural person
sub_obligations.plain_summary: A DPIA is required for systematic, extensive automated evaluation/profiling that drives significant decisions about people.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Where such automated evaluation/profiling occurs, does the policy confirm a DPIA was conducted?

sub_obligations.legal_text: processing on a large scale of special categories of data referred to in Article 9(1), or of personal data relating to criminal convictions and offences referred to in Article 10
sub_obligations.plain_summary: A DPIA is required for large-scale processing of sensitive or criminal data.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Where large-scale special category or criminal data processing occurs, does the policy confirm a DPIA was conducted?

sub_obligations.legal_text: a systematic monitoring of a publicly accessible area on a large scale
sub_obligations.plain_summary: A DPIA is required for large-scale systematic monitoring of public spaces.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Where large-scale public area monitoring occurs, does the policy confirm a DPIA was conducted?

assessment_rules.met_when: Where AT LEAST ONE of the high-risk trigger conditions applies, the policy confirms a DPIA was carried out prior to that processing.
assessment_rules.partially_met_when: High-risk processing is acknowledged but it's unclear whether a DPIA was actually conducted.
assessment_rules.not_met_when: A trigger condition applies and no DPIA process is described.
assessment_rules.conflicting_when: The policy states DPIAs are never conducted regardless of processing risk.
assessment_rules.insufficient_evidence_when: It cannot be determined whether the controller's processing meets any of the high-risk trigger conditions.

requirement_groups.principle: Seeking DPO advice during a DPIA
requirement_groups.requirement_summary: The controller must seek the advice of the DPO, where designated, when carrying out a DPIA.
requirement_groups.applicability_condition: Applies only where a DPIA is being carried out and a DPO has been designated.

sub_obligations.legal_text: The controller shall seek the advice of the data protection officer, where designated, when carrying out a data protection impact assessment.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: If there's a DPO, their advice must be sought during a DPIA.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Where a DPO exists and a DPIA is conducted, does the policy confirm the DPO's advice is sought?

expected_evidence: DPIA process documentation referencing DPO involvement

assessment_rules.met_when: Where a DPO exists and a DPIA is conducted, the policy confirms the DPO's advice is sought.
assessment_rules.partially_met_when: A DPIA process is described without mentioning DPO involvement despite a DPO existing.
assessment_rules.not_met_when: No DPO consultation is described despite both a DPO and DPIA process existing.
assessment_rules.conflicting_when: The policy states DPIAs are conducted without any DPO involvement despite having a designated DPO.
assessment_rules.insufficient_evidence_when: It cannot be determined whether a DPO is designated or involved in DPIAs.

requirement_groups.principle: Required content of a DPIA
requirement_groups.requirement_summary: A DPIA must contain at least a systematic description of the envisaged processing and purposes (including legitimate interests where applicable), a necessity/proportionality assessment, a risk assessment, and the measures envisaged to address the risks.
requirement_groups.applicability_condition: Applies where a DPIA is required and conducted.

sub_obligations.legal_text: a systematic description of the envisaged processing operations and the purposes of the processing, including, where applicable, the legitimate interest pursued by the controller
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The DPIA must systematically describe the processing and its purposes, including any legitimate interests.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy confirm the DPIA process includes a systematic description of processing operations and purposes?

sub_obligations.legal_text: an assessment of the necessity and proportionality of the processing operations in relation to the purposes
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The DPIA must assess whether the processing is necessary and proportionate to its purposes.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy confirm the DPIA includes a necessity and proportionality assessment?

sub_obligations.legal_text: an assessment of the risks to the rights and freedoms of data subjects referred to in paragraph 1
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The DPIA must assess risks to data subjects' rights and freedoms.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy confirm the DPIA includes a risk assessment for data subjects?

sub_obligations.legal_text: the measures envisaged to address the risks, including safeguards, security measures and mechanisms to ensure the protection of personal data and to demonstrate compliance
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The DPIA must identify measures to address the identified risks, including safeguards and security measures.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy confirm the DPIA includes risk-mitigation measures and safeguards?

assessment_rules.met_when: Where a DPIA is conducted, the policy confirms it includes ALL required content elements (a-d).
assessment_rules.partially_met_when: A DPIA process exists but does not clearly cover all required content elements.
assessment_rules.not_met_when: No DPIA content requirements are described despite a DPIA process existing.
assessment_rules.conflicting_when: The policy describes a DPIA process that omits risk assessment or mitigation measures entirely.
assessment_rules.insufficient_evidence_when: It cannot be determined what content the DPIA process covers.

requirement_groups.principle: Stakeholder input, exemption, and ongoing review of DPIAs
requirement_groups.requirement_summary: Where appropriate, the controller must seek the views of data subjects or their representatives; the DPIA obligation does not apply where an equivalent assessment was already carried out as part of a general legislative impact assessment (unless Member States require one anyway); and the controller must review the DPIA when the risk represented by the processing changes.
requirement_groups.applicability_condition: The exemption in 35.10 applies only to processing based on Article 6(1)(c) or (e) with a legal basis already subject to a general impact assessment.

sub_obligations.legal_text: Where appropriate, the controller shall seek the views of data subjects or their representatives on the intended processing, without prejudice to the protection of commercial or public interests or the security of processing operations.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: Where appropriate, the company should get input from data subjects or their representatives on the planned processing.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy indicate that data subject or representative views are sought during the DPIA process where appropriate?

sub_obligations.legal_text: Where processing pursuant to point (c) or (e) of Article 6(1) has a legal basis in Union law or in the law of the Member State...and a data protection impact assessment has already been carried out as part of a general impact assessment...paragraphs 1 to 7 shall not apply unless Member States deem it to be necessary
sub_obligations.plain_summary: A separate DPIA isn't needed if an equivalent assessment was already done as part of adopting the underlying law, unless the Member State still requires one.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Where this exemption is relied on, does the policy identify the legislative impact assessment that substitutes for a separate DPIA?

sub_obligations.legal_text: Where necessary, the controller shall carry out a review to assess if processing is performed in accordance with the data protection impact assessment at least when there is a change of the risk represented by processing operations.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The company must review whether processing still matches its DPIA, at least when the risk level changes.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy commit to reviewing the DPIA when the risk of processing changes?

assessment_rules.met_when: The policy satisfies ALL applicable sub-obligations: stakeholder views are sought where appropriate, any exemption relied upon is properly grounded, and DPIAs are reviewed when risk changes.
assessment_rules.partially_met_when: Some elements (e.g., review commitment) are addressed while others (e.g., stakeholder input) are not.
assessment_rules.not_met_when: None of these elements are addressed despite DPIAs being conducted.
assessment_rules.conflicting_when: The policy claims the legislative exemption without identifying any underlying legislative impact assessment.
assessment_rules.insufficient_evidence_when: It cannot be determined whether stakeholder input is sought, an exemption applies, or reviews occur.

requirement_groups.principle: Obligation to consult the supervisory authority before high-risk processing
requirement_groups.requirement_summary: The controller must consult the supervisory authority prior to processing where a DPIA indicates the processing would result in high risk absent mitigating measures.
requirement_groups.applicability_condition: Applies only where a DPIA indicates residual high risk despite the controller's mitigation measures.

sub_obligations.legal_text: The controller shall consult the supervisory authority prior to processing where a data protection impact assessment under Article 35 indicates that the processing would result in a high risk in the absence of measures taken by the controller to mitigate the risk.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: If a DPIA shows high residual risk, the company must consult the regulator before processing.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Where a DPIA indicates high residual risk, does the policy commit to consulting the supervisory authority before proceeding?

expected_evidence: Prior consultation trigger and procedure description

assessment_rules.met_when: Where high residual risk is indicated by a DPIA, the policy commits to consulting the supervisory authority before processing.
assessment_rules.partially_met_when: DPIA and consultation are both mentioned but the trigger condition for consultation is unclear.
assessment_rules.not_met_when: No prior consultation process is described despite high-risk DPIA outcomes.
assessment_rules.conflicting_when: The policy states processing proceeds regardless of DPIA outcomes without consultation.
assessment_rules.insufficient_evidence_when: It cannot be determined whether any DPIA has identified high residual risk requiring consultation.

requirement_groups.principle: Information to be provided during prior consultation
requirement_groups.requirement_summary: When consulting the supervisory authority, the controller must provide, as applicable, the respective responsibilities of controllers/processors, the purposes and means of the intended processing, the safeguards and measures provided, DPO contact details where applicable, the DPIA, and any other information requested.
requirement_groups.applicability_condition: Applies only where a prior consultation with the supervisory authority is undertaken.

sub_obligations.legal_text: where applicable, the respective responsibilities of the controller, joint controllers and processors involved in the processing, in particular for processing within a group of undertakings
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The consultation must include the roles of each party involved, especially within corporate groups.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: During prior consultation, does the policy indicate the respective responsibilities of involved parties are disclosed?

sub_obligations.legal_text: the purposes and means of the intended processing
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The consultation must describe the purposes and methods of the intended processing.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy indicate the purposes and means of the intended processing are disclosed during consultation?

sub_obligations.legal_text: the measures and safeguards provided to protect the rights and freedoms of data subjects pursuant to this Regulation
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The consultation must describe safeguards protecting data subjects' rights.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy indicate that protective measures and safeguards are disclosed during consultation?

sub_obligations.legal_text: where applicable, the contact details of the data protection officer
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The consultation must include DPO contact details, where applicable.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy indicate DPO contact details are provided during consultation, where applicable?

sub_obligations.legal_text: the data protection impact assessment provided for in Article 35
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The consultation must include the DPIA itself.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy indicate the DPIA is provided to the supervisory authority during consultation?

sub_obligations.legal_text: any other information requested by the supervisory authority
sub_obligations.plain_summary: Any additional information the supervisory authority requests must be provided.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy indicate a commitment to providing additional information requested by the supervisory authority?

assessment_rules.met_when: Where prior consultation is undertaken, the policy confirms ALL required information elements (a-f) are provided.
assessment_rules.partially_met_when: Consultation is described but not all required content elements are addressed.
assessment_rules.not_met_when: No content requirements are described for prior consultation.
assessment_rules.conflicting_when: The policy states the DPIA or safeguards are withheld from the supervisory authority during consultation.
assessment_rules.insufficient_evidence_when: It cannot be determined what information is provided during any prior consultation.

requirement_groups.principle: Member State law requiring prior authorisation for public-interest processing
requirement_groups.requirement_summary: Member State law may require controllers to consult with and obtain prior authorisation from the supervisory authority for processing performed for a public-interest task, including social protection and public health processing.
requirement_groups.applicability_condition: Applies only where the controller performs a public-interest task and applicable Member State law imposes a prior-authorisation requirement.

sub_obligations.legal_text: Member State law may require controllers to consult with, and obtain prior authorisation from, the supervisory authority in relation to processing by a controller for the performance of a task carried out by the controller in the public interest, including processing in relation to social protection and public health.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: Some countries' laws require public-interest processing (like social protection or public health) to get prior regulatory authorisation.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Where applicable Member State law requires it, does the policy confirm prior authorisation is obtained for public-interest processing?

expected_evidence: Prior authorisation statement for public-interest processing

assessment_rules.met_when: Where applicable Member State law requires prior authorisation for public-interest processing, the policy confirms it is obtained.
assessment_rules.partially_met_when: Public-interest processing is described but prior-authorisation status is unclear.
assessment_rules.not_met_when: Applicable law requires prior authorisation and none is obtained.
assessment_rules.conflicting_when: The policy states public-interest processing proceeds without required prior authorisation.
assessment_rules.insufficient_evidence_when: It cannot be determined whether applicable Member State law imposes a prior-authorisation requirement on the controller.

article.title: Designation of the data protection officer

requirement_groups.principle: Mandatory DPO designation triggers
requirement_groups.requirement_summary: A DPO must be designated where the processing is carried out by a public authority or body (except courts acting judicially), where core activities require regular and systematic large-scale monitoring of data subjects, or where core activities involve large-scale processing of special category or criminal conviction/offence data.

sub_obligations.legal_text: the processing is carried out by a public authority or body, except for courts acting in their judicial capacity
sub_obligations.plain_summary: Public authorities/bodies (other than courts acting judicially) must appoint a DPO.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Where the controller is a public authority or body, does the policy confirm a DPO has been designated?

sub_obligations.legal_text: the core activities of the controller or the processor consist of processing operations which, by virtue of their nature, their scope and/or their purposes, require regular and systematic monitoring of data subjects on a large scale
sub_obligations.plain_summary: Organizations whose core business involves large-scale, regular monitoring of people must appoint a DPO.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Where core activities involve large-scale regular systematic monitoring, does the policy confirm a DPO has been designated?

sub_obligations.legal_text: the core activities of the controller or the processor consist of processing on a large scale of special categories of data pursuant to Article 9 and personal data relating to criminal convictions and offences referred to in Article 10
sub_obligations.plain_summary: Organizations whose core business involves large-scale sensitive or criminal data must appoint a DPO.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Where core activities involve large-scale special category or criminal data processing, does the policy confirm a DPO has been designated?

assessment_rules.met_when: Where AT LEAST ONE trigger condition applies, the policy confirms a DPO has been designated.
assessment_rules.partially_met_when: A trigger condition applies but DPO designation status is unclear.
assessment_rules.not_met_when: A trigger condition clearly applies and no DPO is designated.
assessment_rules.conflicting_when: The policy states no DPO is designated despite explicitly describing large-scale monitoring or sensitive data processing as a core activity.
assessment_rules.insufficient_evidence_when: It cannot be determined whether any of the three trigger conditions apply to the controller.

requirement_groups.principle: Flexible DPO designation arrangements
requirement_groups.requirement_summary: A group of undertakings may appoint a single, easily accessible DPO; public authorities/bodies may share a single DPO; and in cases not otherwise mandatory, a DPO may (or, where required by law, shall) be designated, including by associations representing controllers/processors.
requirement_groups.applicability_condition: Applies where the controller is part of a group of undertakings, a public authority sharing a DPO, or voluntarily/legally designating a DPO outside the mandatory triggers.

sub_obligations.legal_text: A group of undertakings may appoint a single data protection officer provided that a data protection officer is easily accessible from each establishment...a single data protection officer may be designated for several such authorities or bodies...the controller or processor or associations...may or, where required by Union or Member State law shall, designate a data protection officer
sub_obligations.plain_summary: Corporate groups and public bodies can share one accessible DPO, and other organizations may (or in some cases must, under national law) appoint one too.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Where a shared or voluntary DPO arrangement exists, does the policy describe it and confirm accessibility where relevant?

expected_evidence: DPO arrangement description for corporate groups or shared authorities

assessment_rules.met_when: Where a shared or voluntary DPO arrangement exists, the policy describes it, confirming accessibility for group/shared arrangements.
assessment_rules.partially_met_when: A shared DPO is mentioned without confirming accessibility from each establishment.
assessment_rules.not_met_when: Not applicable in the ordinary case; only relevant where the controller relies on one of these flexible arrangements without proper implementation.
assessment_rules.conflicting_when: The policy describes a shared DPO who is not accessible from a relevant establishment.
assessment_rules.insufficient_evidence_when: It cannot be determined whether the controller uses a shared or voluntary DPO arrangement.

requirement_groups.principle: DPO qualifications and engagement basis
requirement_groups.requirement_summary: The DPO must be designated based on professional qualities, in particular expert knowledge of data protection law/practices and the ability to fulfil their tasks, and may be a staff member or engaged under a service contract.
requirement_groups.applicability_condition: Applies wherever a DPO is designated.

sub_obligations.legal_text: The data protection officer shall be designated on the basis of professional qualities and, in particular, expert knowledge of data protection law and practices and the ability to fulfil the tasks referred to in Article 39.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The DPO must be chosen for their expertise in data protection law and ability to do the job.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy confirm the DPO was selected based on relevant expertise and ability to fulfil their tasks?

sub_obligations.legal_text: The data protection officer may be a staff member of the controller or processor, or fulfil the tasks on the basis of a service contract.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The DPO can be an internal employee or an outsourced contractor.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy indicate whether the DPO is an internal staff member or engaged via a service contract?

expected_evidence: DPO qualifications and engagement basis description

assessment_rules.met_when: Where a DPO is designated, the policy satisfies ALL sub-obligations: expertise-based selection and clarity on engagement basis.
assessment_rules.partially_met_when: The DPO's role is identified but qualifications or engagement basis are not described.
assessment_rules.not_met_when: A DPO is designated with no information on qualifications or engagement basis.
assessment_rules.conflicting_when: The policy describes a DPO role filled without regard to data protection expertise.
assessment_rules.insufficient_evidence_when: It cannot be determined whether a DPO is designated at all.

requirement_groups.principle: Publication and communication of DPO contact details
requirement_groups.requirement_summary: The controller/processor must publish the DPO's contact details and communicate them to the supervisory authority.
requirement_groups.applicability_condition: Applies wherever a DPO is designated.

sub_obligations.legal_text: The controller or the processor shall publish the contact details of the data protection officer
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The DPO's contact details must be made public.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy publish the DPO's contact details, where a DPO is designated?

sub_obligations.legal_text: and communicate them to the supervisory authority
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The DPO's contact details must also be reported to the supervisory authority.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy indicate the DPO's contact details are communicated to the supervisory authority?

expected_evidence: Published DPO contact details in the policy

assessment_rules.met_when: Where a DPO is designated, the policy satisfies ALL sub-obligations: DPO contact details are published and reported to the supervisory authority.
assessment_rules.partially_met_when: DPO contact details are published but no indication is given of reporting to the supervisory authority, or vice versa.
assessment_rules.not_met_when: A DPO is designated but contact details are neither published nor reported.
assessment_rules.conflicting_when: The policy states DPO contact details are kept confidential from the public.
assessment_rules.insufficient_evidence_when: It cannot be determined whether a DPO is designated or whether contact details are published/reported.

article.title: Position of the data protection officer

requirement_groups.principle: Timely involvement and support of the DPO
requirement_groups.requirement_summary: The controller/processor must ensure the DPO is properly and timely involved in all data-protection-related issues, and must support the DPO with necessary resources, access to data/processing operations, and opportunities to maintain expertise.
requirement_groups.applicability_condition: Applies wherever a DPO is designated.

sub_obligations.legal_text: The controller and the processor shall ensure that the data protection officer is involved, properly and in a timely manner, in all issues which relate to the protection of personal data.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The DPO must be brought into all relevant data protection matters early and properly.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy confirm the DPO is properly and timely involved in all data protection issues?

sub_obligations.legal_text: The controller and processor shall support the data protection officer in performing the tasks referred to in Article 39 by providing resources necessary to carry out those tasks and access to personal data and processing operations, and to maintain his or her expert knowledge.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The DPO must be given the resources, data access, and ongoing training needed to do their job.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy confirm the DPO is given necessary resources, data access, and support to maintain expertise?

assessment_rules.met_when: Where a DPO is designated, the policy satisfies ALL sub-obligations: proper timely involvement and adequate resourcing/access/training.
assessment_rules.partially_met_when: One aspect (involvement or support) is addressed while the other is not.
assessment_rules.not_met_when: Neither involvement nor support commitments are described despite a DPO being designated.
assessment_rules.conflicting_when: The policy states the DPO is excluded from relevant data protection decisions or denied resources.
assessment_rules.insufficient_evidence_when: It cannot be determined whether a DPO is designated or how they are involved/supported.

requirement_groups.principle: DPO independence and protection
requirement_groups.requirement_summary: The DPO must not receive instructions regarding the exercise of their tasks, must not be dismissed or penalised for performing their tasks, and must report directly to the highest management level.
requirement_groups.applicability_condition: Applies wherever a DPO is designated.

sub_obligations.legal_text: The controller and processor shall ensure that the data protection officer does not receive any instructions regarding the exercise of those tasks.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The DPO must be free to carry out their tasks without being directed by others.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy confirm the DPO acts independently, without instructions regarding task performance?

sub_obligations.legal_text: He or she shall not be dismissed or penalised by the controller or the processor for performing his tasks.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The DPO cannot be fired or punished for doing their job.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy confirm the DPO is protected from dismissal or penalty for performing their tasks?

sub_obligations.legal_text: The data protection officer shall directly report to the highest management level of the controller or the processor.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The DPO must report directly to top leadership.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy confirm the DPO reports directly to the highest level of management?

expected_evidence: DPO independence and reporting structure statement

assessment_rules.met_when: Where a DPO is designated, the policy satisfies ALL sub-obligations: independence, protection from dismissal/penalty, and direct reporting to top management.
assessment_rules.partially_met_when: Some but not all of these protections are described.
assessment_rules.not_met_when: None of these protections are described despite a DPO being designated.
assessment_rules.conflicting_when: The policy states the DPO reports to a mid-level manager or can be dismissed for their DPO activities.
assessment_rules.insufficient_evidence_when: It cannot be determined whether these independence protections apply to the designated DPO.

requirement_groups.principle: Data subject access to the DPO and DPO confidentiality
requirement_groups.requirement_summary: Data subjects may contact the DPO on all issues related to their data processing and rights, and the DPO must be bound by secrecy or confidentiality regarding the performance of their tasks.
requirement_groups.applicability_condition: Applies wherever a DPO is designated.

sub_obligations.legal_text: Data subjects may contact the data protection officer with regard to all issues related to processing of their personal data and to the exercise of their rights under this Regulation.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: People can reach out to the DPO about their data or their rights.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy confirm data subjects can contact the DPO regarding their data processing and rights?

sub_obligations.legal_text: The data protection officer shall be bound by secrecy or confidentiality concerning the performance of his or her tasks, in accordance with Union or Member State law.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The DPO must keep confidentiality in carrying out their duties, per applicable law.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy confirm the DPO is bound by secrecy or confidentiality obligations regarding their tasks?

assessment_rules.met_when: Where a DPO is designated, the policy satisfies ALL sub-obligations: an accessible contact channel for data subjects and a confidentiality obligation for the DPO.
assessment_rules.partially_met_when: One element is addressed while the other is not.
assessment_rules.not_met_when: Neither element is addressed despite a DPO being designated.
assessment_rules.conflicting_when: The policy states data subjects cannot contact the DPO directly, or that the DPO has no confidentiality obligation.
assessment_rules.insufficient_evidence_when: It cannot be determined whether these arrangements are in place for the designated DPO.

requirement_groups.principle: DPO's other tasks must not create conflicts of interest
requirement_groups.requirement_summary: The DPO may fulfil other tasks and duties, but the controller/processor must ensure any such additional tasks do not result in a conflict of interest.
requirement_groups.applicability_condition: Applies where the designated DPO holds additional roles or responsibilities.

sub_obligations.legal_text: The data protection officer may fulfil other tasks and duties. The controller or processor shall ensure that any such tasks and duties do not result in a conflict of interests.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: If the DPO has other job duties, the company must make sure those don't conflict with their DPO role.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Where the DPO holds other roles, does the policy confirm those roles do not create a conflict of interest with DPO duties?

expected_evidence: Conflict-of-interest assessment for the DPO's other duties

assessment_rules.met_when: Where the DPO holds other roles, the policy confirms a conflict-of-interest assessment has been made and no conflict exists.
assessment_rules.partially_met_when: The DPO's other roles are disclosed without a conflict-of-interest assessment.
assessment_rules.not_met_when: The DPO holds other roles (e.g., head of IT or marketing) with no conflict-of-interest safeguard described.
assessment_rules.conflicting_when: The DPO's other role is one that inherently determines the purposes/means of processing (e.g., Chief Marketing Officer), creating an evident conflict acknowledged in the policy.
assessment_rules.insufficient_evidence_when: It cannot be determined whether the DPO holds any other roles within the organisation.

article.title: Tasks of the data protection officer

requirement_groups.principle: Minimum DPO tasks
requirement_groups.requirement_summary: The DPO must at least: inform and advise the controller/processor and employees of their GDPR obligations; monitor compliance including staff training and audits; advise on and monitor DPIAs; cooperate with the supervisory authority; and act as the contact point for the supervisory authority, including on prior consultation.
requirement_groups.applicability_condition: Applies wherever a DPO is designated.

sub_obligations.legal_text: to inform and advise the controller or the processor and the employees who carry out processing of their obligations pursuant to this Regulation and to other Union or Member State data protection provisions
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The DPO must inform and advise the company and staff on their data protection obligations.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy confirm the DPO informs and advises the organisation and staff on data protection obligations?

sub_obligations.legal_text: to monitor compliance with this Regulation...including the assignment of responsibilities, awareness-raising and training of staff involved in processing operations, and the related audits
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The DPO must monitor compliance, including staff training, responsibility assignment, and audits.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy confirm the DPO monitors compliance, including staff training and audits?

sub_obligations.legal_text: to provide advice where requested as regards the data protection impact assessment and monitor its performance pursuant to Article 35
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The DPO must advise on and monitor DPIAs when asked.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy confirm the DPO provides DPIA advice and monitors DPIA performance?

sub_obligations.legal_text: to cooperate with the supervisory authority
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The DPO must cooperate with the supervisory authority.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy confirm the DPO cooperates with the supervisory authority?

sub_obligations.legal_text: to act as the contact point for the supervisory authority on issues relating to processing, including the prior consultation referred to in Article 36, and to consult, where appropriate, with regard to any other matter
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The DPO acts as the point of contact for the supervisory authority on processing matters, including prior consultation.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy confirm the DPO serves as the contact point for the supervisory authority, including for prior consultation?

assessment_rules.met_when: Where a DPO is designated, the policy confirms ALL of the minimum tasks (a-e) are performed by the DPO.
assessment_rules.partially_met_when: Some but not all of the minimum DPO tasks are described.
assessment_rules.not_met_when: The DPO's tasks are not described at all despite a DPO being designated.
assessment_rules.conflicting_when: The policy describes a DPO role that excludes one of the mandatory minimum tasks (e.g., no supervisory authority contact function).
assessment_rules.insufficient_evidence_when: It cannot be determined what tasks the designated DPO performs.

requirement_groups.principle: Risk-based prioritisation of DPO tasks
requirement_groups.requirement_summary: In performing their tasks, the DPO must have due regard to the risk associated with processing operations, taking into account the nature, scope, context, and purposes of processing.
requirement_groups.applicability_condition: Applies wherever a DPO is designated.

sub_obligations.legal_text: The data protection officer shall in the performance of his or her tasks have due regard to the risk associated with processing operations, taking into account the nature, scope, context and purposes of processing.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The DPO should focus their efforts based on the actual risk level of different processing activities.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy indicate that the DPO's work is prioritised according to the risk level of different processing activities?

assessment_rules.met_when: Where a DPO is designated, the policy indicates the DPO's task performance is informed by the risk level of processing activities.
assessment_rules.partially_met_when: DPO tasks are described generically without reference to risk-based prioritisation.
assessment_rules.not_met_when: The policy does not address how DPO efforts are prioritised at all.
assessment_rules.conflicting_when: The policy states the DPO applies a uniform, non-risk-based approach to all processing regardless of scale or sensitivity.
assessment_rules.insufficient_evidence_when: It cannot be determined how the DPO's work is prioritised or informed by risk.

article.title: Codes of conduct
article.contextual_reason: Article 40 establishes the framework by which industry associations, supervisory authorities, the Board, and the Commission encourage, draft, submit, approve, register, and grant general validity to codes of conduct. The obligations it creates run to associations preparing codes and to regulators approving them, not to an individual controller's own privacy policy. A controller's optional adherence to an already-approved code (addressed briefly in paragraph 3, for cross-border transfer safeguards) is elective and evidentiary rather than a standalone testable requirement, and is more appropriately captured, where relevant, under the transfer-safeguards requirements of Chapter V or the accountability-evidence groups of Article 24/32.

article.title: Monitoring of approved codes of conduct
article.contextual_reason: Article 41 governs the accreditation and functioning of independent monitoring bodies that oversee compliance with approved codes of conduct. Its obligations (demonstrating independence and expertise, establishing complaint-handling procedures, avoiding conflicts of interest, accreditation revocation) apply to the monitoring body itself, not to a controller's privacy policy. It does not apply to processing by public authorities and bodies at all. There is no requirement here that a company's own privacy policy could be checked against.

article.title: Certification
article.contextual_reason: Article 42 establishes the voluntary framework for creating and issuing data protection certification mechanisms, seals, and marks, including the procedures by which supervisory authorities, the Board, and certification bodies approve criteria and issue certifications. Certification itself is explicitly voluntary (Article 42(3)) and does not reduce a controller's underlying compliance responsibility (Article 42(4)) — meaning there is no independent, mandatory obligation here for a privacy policy to satisfy beyond the substantive requirements already captured elsewhere (e.g., Articles 24, 25, 28, 32). Any use of certification as compliance evidence is already captured within the relevant substantive articles' assessment groups.

article.title: Certification bodies
article.contextual_reason: Article 43 sets out the accreditation requirements and procedures for third-party certification bodies that issue GDPR certifications, including their independence, expertise, complaint-handling procedures, and accreditation renewal/revocation. These obligations run to certification bodies and accreditation authorities, not to a controller's own privacy policy, and are not testable against a company's data-handling practices.

chapter.name: Transfers of personal data to third countries or international organisations

requirement_groups.principle: Overarching transfer compliance principle
requirement_groups.requirement_summary: Any transfer of personal data to a third country or international organisation, including onward transfers, may only take place if the conditions in Chapter V are met, and the level of protection guaranteed by the GDPR must not be undermined.
requirement_groups.applicability_condition: Applies whenever the company transfers personal data outside the EU/EEA, including onward transfers by a recipient in a third country to another third country or international organisation.

sub_obligations.legal_text: shall take place only if...the conditions laid down in this Chapter are complied with by the controller and processor, including for onward transfers of personal data from the third country or an international organisation to another third country or to another international organisation
sub_obligations.plain_summary: International transfers, including onward transfers from the recipient country, are only allowed if they meet the conditions in this Chapter.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy state that international transfers, including onward transfers by third-country recipients, only occur when Chapter V conditions are satisfied?

sub_obligations.legal_text: the level of protection of natural persons guaranteed by this Regulation is not undermined
sub_obligations.plain_summary: Transfers must not weaken the data protection guarantees people have under the GDPR.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy commit to ensuring that international transfers do not reduce the level of data protection guaranteed under the GDPR?

expected_evidence: International data transfers section of privacy policy
Onward transfer restrictions in vendor/processor contracts

assessment_rules.met_when: ALL sub-obligations are satisfied: the policy confirms transfers (including onward transfers) only occur under a Chapter V mechanism, and that GDPR-level protection is preserved.
assessment_rules.partially_met_when: The policy addresses one sub-obligation but not the other (e.g., mentions transfer safeguards but is silent on onward transfers, or vice versa).
assessment_rules.not_met_when: The policy allows or describes international transfers with no reference to any Chapter V mechanism or to preserving the level of protection.
assessment_rules.conflicting_when: The policy explicitly permits transfers or onward transfers without any safeguard, adequacy basis, or derogation.
assessment_rules.insufficient_evidence_when: The policy does not describe international transfers at all, so applicability and compliance cannot be determined.

chapter.name: Transfers of personal data to third countries or international organisations

article.title: Transfers on the basis of an adequacy decision

requirement_groups.principle: Transfers under an adequacy decision
requirement_groups.requirement_summary: A transfer to a third country, territory, sector, or international organisation covered by a European Commission adequacy decision may take place without any specific additional authorisation.
requirement_groups.applicability_condition: Applies only where the company transfers personal data to a destination currently covered by an EU Commission adequacy decision.

sub_obligations.legal_text: A transfer of personal data to a third country or an international organisation may take place where the Commission has decided that...the international organisation in question ensures an adequate level of protection...Such a transfer shall not require any specific authorisation.
sub_obligations.plain_summary: If the Commission has recognised a country, sector, or organisation as offering adequate protection, transfers there don't need extra authorisation.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy identify transfers to adequacy-decision countries and state that no additional transfer safeguard or authorisation is required for those transfers?

expected_evidence: International transfers section listing adequacy-decision destinations

assessment_rules.met_when: The single sub-obligation is satisfied: the policy correctly identifies that transfers to adequacy-decision destinations rely on that decision and require no further authorisation.
assessment_rules.partially_met_when: The policy mentions adequacy decisions generally but does not clearly identify which destinations or processing this covers.
assessment_rules.not_met_when: The policy either does not mention adequacy decisions at all where relevant, or requires unnecessary additional safeguards for adequacy-covered destinations without explanation.
assessment_rules.conflicting_when: The policy states that no safeguards of any kind apply to a destination that is not actually subject to a current Commission adequacy decision.
assessment_rules.insufficient_evidence_when: The policy does not specify which countries or organisations data is transferred to, so reliance on adequacy cannot be assessed.

requirement_groups.principle: Monitoring adequacy status changes
requirement_groups.requirement_summary: Because the Commission can amend, suspend, or repeal an adequacy decision, a company relying on one should have a process to detect and respond to such changes.
requirement_groups.applicability_condition: Applies only where the company relies on an adequacy decision as its transfer mechanism.

sub_obligations.legal_text: the Commission shall...repeal, amend or suspend the decision...without retro-active effect
sub_obligations.plain_summary: Adequacy decisions can be changed or withdrawn, which would remove the legal basis for transfers relying on them.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy or internal process describe how the company monitors for changes to relevant adequacy decisions and what it will do if one is repealed or suspended?

expected_evidence: Vendor management policy referencing adequacy status review

assessment_rules.met_when: The single sub-obligation is satisfied: there is a documented process for monitoring adequacy decision status and switching transfer mechanisms if it changes.
assessment_rules.partially_met_when: The company acknowledges adequacy decisions can change but has no defined monitoring or contingency process.
assessment_rules.not_met_when: There is no acknowledgment that adequacy decisions are reviewable or subject to change.
assessment_rules.conflicting_when: Not applicable to this group (no scenario where the policy would explicitly contradict this).
assessment_rules.insufficient_evidence_when: The policy provides no information about ongoing governance of transfer mechanisms.

chapter.name: Transfers of personal data to third countries or international organisations

requirement_groups.principle: Core safeguard requirement absent an adequacy decision
requirement_groups.requirement_summary: Where no adequacy decision applies, a transfer may only occur if the controller/processor has provided appropriate safeguards AND enforceable data subject rights and effective legal remedies are available.
requirement_groups.applicability_condition: Applies where the destination is not covered by an Article 45(3) adequacy decision.

sub_obligations.legal_text: the controller or processor has provided appropriate safeguards
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The company must put a recognised safeguard mechanism in place before transferring data.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy state that appropriate safeguards are put in place before transferring personal data to non-adequate countries?

sub_obligations.legal_text: on condition that enforceable data subject rights and effective legal remedies for data subjects are available
sub_obligations.plain_summary: People must still be able to enforce their rights and get legal redress after the transfer.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy confirm that data subjects retain enforceable rights and access to effective legal remedies after such a transfer?

assessment_rules.met_when: ALL sub-obligations are satisfied: a recognised safeguard is used AND the policy confirms enforceable rights and effective remedies remain available.
assessment_rules.partially_met_when: A safeguard mechanism is named but nothing is said about preserved enforceable rights/remedies, or vice versa.
assessment_rules.not_met_when: Transfers to non-adequate countries are described with no safeguard mechanism identified.
assessment_rules.conflicting_when: The policy explicitly transfers data to non-adequate countries without any safeguard and states data subjects have no recourse.
assessment_rules.insufficient_evidence_when: The policy does not specify whether destinations are adequacy-covered or not, so this group's applicability cannot be determined.

requirement_groups.principle: Safeguard mechanisms not requiring supervisory authorisation
requirement_groups.requirement_summary: Appropriate safeguards under 46.1 can be provided by any one of several pre-approved mechanisms that do not need case-by-case supervisory authority sign-off.
requirement_groups.applicability_condition: Applies when the company relies on Article 46 safeguards (see group 46.1) rather than an adequacy decision.

sub_obligations.legal_text: a legally binding and enforceable instrument between public authorities or bodies
sub_obligations.plain_summary: A binding agreement between public authorities can serve as a safeguard.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy reference a legally binding instrument between public authorities as its transfer safeguard, where relevant?

sub_obligations.legal_text: binding corporate rules in accordance with Article 47
sub_obligations.plain_summary: Approved binding corporate rules within a corporate group can serve as a safeguard.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy reference approved Binding Corporate Rules as a transfer safeguard?

sub_obligations.legal_text: standard data protection clauses adopted by the Commission
sub_obligations.plain_summary: EU Commission-approved standard contractual clauses (SCCs) can serve as a safeguard.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy reference Commission-adopted Standard Contractual Clauses as a transfer safeguard?

sub_obligations.legal_text: standard data protection clauses adopted by a supervisory authority and approved by the Commission
sub_obligations.plain_summary: Supervisory-authority-issued SCCs, approved by the Commission, can serve as a safeguard.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy reference supervisory-authority-adopted, Commission-approved standard clauses as a transfer safeguard?

sub_obligations.legal_text: an approved code of conduct pursuant to Article 40 together with binding and enforceable commitments...to apply the appropriate safeguards
sub_obligations.plain_summary: An approved code of conduct with binding commitments can serve as a safeguard.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy reference an approved code of conduct with binding commitments as its transfer safeguard?

sub_obligations.legal_text: an approved certification mechanism pursuant to Article 42 together with binding and enforceable commitments...to apply the appropriate safeguards
sub_obligations.plain_summary: An approved certification mechanism with binding commitments can serve as a safeguard.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy reference an approved certification mechanism with binding commitments as its transfer safeguard?

expected_evidence: Code of conduct or certification commitments

assessment_rules.met_when: AT LEAST ONE sub-obligation is satisfied: the policy identifies use of at least one of the listed mechanisms for a given transfer.
assessment_rules.partially_met_when: A mechanism is named in general terms (e.g., 'we use standard contractual clauses') without being tied to specific transfers or recipients.
assessment_rules.not_met_when: No mechanism from this list is identified for a transfer that requires one.
assessment_rules.conflicting_when: The policy states transfers occur using none of these mechanisms and no supervisory-authorised alternative (see group 46.3) either.
assessment_rules.insufficient_evidence_when: The policy does not describe how transfers to non-adequate countries are safeguarded at all.

requirement_groups.principle: Safeguard mechanisms requiring supervisory authorisation
requirement_groups.requirement_summary: As an alternative to the mechanisms in 46.2, safeguards may also be provided through ad hoc contractual clauses or administrative arrangements, but only with authorisation from the competent supervisory authority.
requirement_groups.applicability_condition: Applies only where the company uses ad hoc contractual clauses or administrative arrangements (rather than the pre-approved mechanisms in group 46.2) as its transfer safeguard.

sub_obligations.legal_text: contractual clauses between the controller or processor and the controller, processor or the recipient of the personal data in the third country or international organisation
sub_obligations.plain_summary: Custom contract clauses with the recipient, authorised by a supervisory authority, can serve as a safeguard.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy reference supervisory-authority-authorised ad hoc contractual clauses as its transfer safeguard?

sub_obligations.legal_text: provisions to be inserted into administrative arrangements between public authorities or bodies which include enforceable and effective data subject rights
sub_obligations.plain_summary: Authorised administrative arrangements between public bodies, including enforceable rights, can serve as a safeguard.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy reference authorised administrative arrangements between public bodies, including enforceable data subject rights, as its transfer safeguard?

assessment_rules.met_when: AT LEAST ONE sub-obligation is satisfied AND the company can show the relevant supervisory authority authorisation was obtained.
assessment_rules.partially_met_when: A relevant clause or arrangement is described but no evidence of supervisory authority authorisation is provided.
assessment_rules.not_met_when: The company relies on ad hoc clauses or administrative arrangements without any authorisation.
assessment_rules.conflicting_when: The policy states such clauses are used without supervisory authorisation, contrary to the requirement.
assessment_rules.insufficient_evidence_when: The policy does not indicate whether any transfer relies on this route at all.

chapter.name: Transfers of personal data to third countries or international organisations

requirement_groups.principle: Baseline conditions for approved BCRs
requirement_groups.requirement_summary: For binding corporate rules (BCRs) to be approved, they must be legally binding on and enforced by every group member and their employees, must expressly confer enforceable rights on data subjects, and must contain the mandatory content set out in Article 47(2).
requirement_groups.applicability_condition: Applies only if the company, as part of a corporate group, relies on approved Binding Corporate Rules for intra-group international transfers.

sub_obligations.legal_text: are legally binding and apply to and are enforced by every member concerned of the group of undertakings...including their employees
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The BCRs must bind and be enforced against every relevant group company and its staff.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy confirm the BCRs are legally binding on and enforced by every relevant group entity and employee?

sub_obligations.legal_text: expressly confer enforceable rights on data subjects with regard to the processing of their personal data
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The BCRs must give people enforceable rights they can act on.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy state that the BCRs give data subjects directly enforceable rights?

assessment_rules.met_when: ALL sub-obligations here are satisfied AND group 47.2's content requirements are also met.
assessment_rules.partially_met_when: The BCRs are referenced but binding effect on all members or enforceable data subject rights is not clearly demonstrated.
assessment_rules.not_met_when: The company claims to rely on BCRs but they are not binding on all group members or confer no enforceable rights.
assessment_rules.conflicting_when: The BCRs explicitly exclude certain group members or employees from being bound, or deny data subjects enforceable rights.
assessment_rules.insufficient_evidence_when: The policy mentions BCRs without providing the underlying BCR document or approval evidence.

requirement_groups.principle: Mandatory BCR content
requirement_groups.requirement_summary: Approved BCRs must specify a defined set of elements covering group structure, transfer scope, legal effect, data protection principles, data subject rights, liability, transparency, governance, complaint-handling, auditing, change reporting, and training.
requirement_groups.applicability_condition: Applies only where the company relies on Binding Corporate Rules (same condition as group 47.1).

sub_obligations.legal_text: the structure and contact details of the group of undertakings...and of each of its members
sub_obligations.plain_summary: BCRs must list the group's structure and each member's contact details.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Do the BCRs specify the group structure and contact details of each member?

sub_obligations.legal_text: the data transfers or set of transfers, including the categories of personal data, the type of processing and its purposes, the type of data subjects affected and the identification of the third country or countries in question
sub_obligations.plain_summary: BCRs must describe exactly what data is transferred, why, to whom it relates, and to which countries.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Do the BCRs describe the categories of data, processing purposes, affected data subjects, and destination countries covered?

sub_obligations.legal_text: their legally binding nature, both internally and externally...the application of the general data protection principles...the rights of data subjects in regard to processing and the means to exercise those rights
sub_obligations.plain_summary: BCRs must state their binding legal effect, apply core GDPR principles, and set out data subject rights and how to exercise them, including rights related to automated decision-making and complaints.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Do the BCRs confirm their binding legal effect, apply GDPR principles such as purpose limitation and data minimisation, and explain data subject rights including complaint and redress routes?

sub_obligations.legal_text: the acceptance by the controller or processor established on the territory of a Member State of liability for any breaches of the binding corporate rules by any member concerned not established in the Union
sub_obligations.plain_summary: An EU-based group member must accept liability for BCR breaches by non-EU members.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Do the BCRs specify that an EU-established group member accepts liability for breaches by non-EU members?

sub_obligations.legal_text: how the information on the binding corporate rules...is provided to the data subjects in addition to Articles 13 and 14
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The BCRs must explain how their content is communicated to data subjects, beyond standard privacy notices.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Do the BCRs describe how their content is communicated to data subjects in addition to standard Article 13/14 notices?

sub_obligations.legal_text: the tasks of any data protection officer...in charge of the monitoring compliance...the complaint procedures...the mechanisms...for ensuring the verification of compliance...the mechanisms for reporting and recording changes to the rules...the cooperation mechanism with the supervisory authority...the mechanisms for reporting...any legal requirements...likely to have a substantial adverse effect
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The BCRs must define governance: compliance monitoring roles, complaint procedures, audit/verification mechanisms, a process for reporting rule changes, cooperation with supervisory authorities, and a process for reporting conflicting third-country legal requirements.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Do the BCRs define compliance monitoring responsibility, complaint handling, audit mechanisms, rule-change reporting, supervisory authority cooperation, and reporting of conflicting foreign legal requirements?

sub_obligations.legal_text: the appropriate data protection training to personnel having permanent or regular access to personal data
sub_obligations.plain_summary: Staff who regularly access personal data must receive appropriate data protection training.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Do the BCRs commit to data protection training for personnel with regular access to personal data?

expected_evidence: BCR approval decision from lead supervisory authority

assessment_rules.met_when: ALL sub-obligations are satisfied: every mandatory content element from Article 47(2) is present in the BCRs.
assessment_rules.partially_met_when: Some mandatory content elements are present but others (e.g., liability acceptance, training, or audit mechanisms) are missing.
assessment_rules.not_met_when: The BCRs omit most or all of the mandatory content elements.
assessment_rules.conflicting_when: The BCRs explicitly exclude a required element, such as denying liability acceptance by the EU entity.
assessment_rules.insufficient_evidence_when: The full text of the BCRs is not available for review against this checklist.

chapter.name: Transfers of personal data to third countries or international organisations

article.title: Transfers or disclosures not authorised by Union law

requirement_groups.principle: Foreign judgment/order recognition limited to international agreements
requirement_groups.requirement_summary: A foreign court judgment or administrative decision demanding transfer or disclosure of personal data may only be recognised or enforced if based on an applicable international agreement (e.g., a mutual legal assistance treaty) between the requesting third country and the EU or a Member State, without prejudice to other Chapter V transfer grounds.
requirement_groups.applicability_condition: Applies whenever the company may receive data disclosure or transfer demands from foreign courts, regulators, or law enforcement.

sub_obligations.legal_text: Any judgment of a court or tribunal and any decision of an administrative authority of a third country requiring a controller or processor to transfer or disclose personal data may only be recognised or enforceable in any manner if based on an international agreement...in force between the requesting third country and the Union or a Member State
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The company should not automatically comply with a foreign court or authority's demand to hand over personal data unless it is backed by a relevant international agreement, without prejudice to other valid transfer grounds.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy state that requests from foreign courts or authorities for personal data are only complied with if grounded in a relevant international agreement (such as an MLAT), or another valid Chapter V transfer basis?

expected_evidence: Legal team escalation process for foreign data requests

assessment_rules.met_when: The single sub-obligation is satisfied: the policy commits to only recognising/complying with foreign data demands based on an applicable international agreement or another valid transfer basis under this Chapter.
assessment_rules.partially_met_when: The policy generally mentions handling government/legal requests but does not specifically condition compliance on an international agreement or other Chapter V basis.
assessment_rules.not_met_when: The policy is silent on how foreign court or administrative demands for data are handled.
assessment_rules.conflicting_when: The policy states it will comply with any foreign court or administrative order regardless of a supporting international agreement.
assessment_rules.insufficient_evidence_when: There is no information about the company's exposure to or process for foreign government/court data requests.

chapter.name: Transfers of personal data to third countries or international organisations

requirement_groups.principle: Derogation grounds absent adequacy decision or safeguards
requirement_groups.requirement_summary: In the absence of an adequacy decision or Article 46 safeguards, a transfer may still take place if at least one of the listed derogation conditions is met.
requirement_groups.applicability_condition: Applies only where no adequacy decision (Article 45) and no appropriate safeguard (Article 46, including BCRs) covers the transfer.

sub_obligations.legal_text: the data subject has explicitly consented to the proposed transfer, after having been informed of the possible risks
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The person gave explicit, informed consent to the specific transfer, including being told about the risks.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy describe obtaining explicit, risk-informed consent as a basis for transfers lacking adequacy or safeguards?

sub_obligations.legal_text: the transfer is necessary for the performance of a contract between the data subject and the controller or the implementation of pre-contractual measures taken at the data subject's request
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The transfer is necessary to perform a contract with the person, or to take pre-contractual steps they requested.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy identify contract performance or pre-contractual steps requested by the data subject as a transfer basis?

sub_obligations.legal_text: the transfer is necessary for the conclusion or performance of a contract concluded in the interest of the data subject between the controller and another natural or legal person
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The transfer is necessary for a contract made in the person's interest with a third party.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy identify contracts made in the data subject's interest with third parties as a transfer basis?

sub_obligations.legal_text: the transfer is necessary for important reasons of public interest
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The transfer is necessary for an important public interest recognised in EU or Member State law.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy identify important public interest reasons, recognised in law, as a transfer basis?

sub_obligations.legal_text: the transfer is necessary for the establishment, exercise or defence of legal claims
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The transfer is necessary to establish, exercise, or defend legal claims.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy identify legal claims (establishment, exercise, or defence) as a transfer basis?

sub_obligations.legal_text: the transfer is necessary in order to protect the vital interests of the data subject or of other persons, where the data subject is physically or legally incapable of giving consent
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The transfer is necessary to protect someone's vital interests when they cannot consent.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy identify protection of vital interests, where consent cannot be given, as a transfer basis?

sub_obligations.legal_text: the transfer is made from a register which according to Union or Member State law is intended to provide information to the public
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The transfer is made from a public register open to consultation, within the legal conditions for that register.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy identify transfers from a public register, made under the register's legal consultation conditions, as a transfer basis?

expected_evidence: International transfers section listing derogations relied upon

assessment_rules.met_when: AT LEAST ONE sub-obligation is satisfied for a given transfer that lacks an adequacy decision or Article 46 safeguard.
assessment_rules.partially_met_when: A derogation is referenced but the necessity or informed-consent element is not clearly demonstrated.
assessment_rules.not_met_when: None of the listed derogations is identified for a transfer lacking adequacy or safeguards.
assessment_rules.conflicting_when: The policy transfers data on a derogation ground that plainly does not fit the stated facts (e.g., claiming 'vital interests' for routine marketing transfers).
assessment_rules.insufficient_evidence_when: The policy does not indicate which, if any, legal basis supports transfers lacking adequacy or safeguards.

requirement_groups.principle: Residual compelling-legitimate-interest derogation
requirement_groups.requirement_summary: Where none of the Article 45/46 mechanisms or the 49.1 derogations apply, a limited, non-repetitive transfer may still occur if it serves compelling legitimate interests not overridden by the data subject's interests, following a documented assessment, with the supervisory authority and data subject informed.
requirement_groups.applicability_condition: Applies only in the narrow case where no adequacy decision, no Article 46 safeguard, and none of the group 49.1 derogations apply to the transfer.

sub_obligations.legal_text: the transfer is not repetitive, concerns only a limited number of data subjects, is necessary for the purposes of compelling legitimate interests pursued by the controller which are not overridden by the interests or rights and freedoms of the data subject
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The transfer must be a one-off, small-scale, and driven by compelling interests that outweigh the person's rights.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy limit this residual transfer basis to non-repetitive, limited-scale transfers where compelling legitimate interests are not overridden by the data subject's rights?

sub_obligations.legal_text: the controller has assessed all the circumstances surrounding the data transfer and has on the basis of that assessment provided suitable safeguards
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The company must document an assessment of the transfer's circumstances and put suitable safeguards in place.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy describe a documented circumstance assessment and suitable safeguards before relying on this residual basis?

sub_obligations.legal_text: The controller shall inform the supervisory authority of the transfer. The controller shall...inform the data subject of the transfer and on the compelling legitimate interests pursued
sub_obligations.plain_summary: The company must notify the supervisory authority and inform the data subject about the transfer and the compelling interests relied on.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy commit to notifying the supervisory authority and informing the data subject when this residual basis is used?

expected_evidence: Transfer assessment documentation for exceptional transfers

assessment_rules.met_when: ALL sub-obligations are satisfied when this residual basis is used: scope limits are respected, an assessment with safeguards is documented, and both the supervisory authority and data subject are informed.
assessment_rules.partially_met_when: The residual basis is used but only some of the required steps (scope limits, assessment, notifications) are documented.
assessment_rules.not_met_when: The residual basis is used with no documented assessment, safeguards, or notifications.
assessment_rules.conflicting_when: The policy uses this basis for repetitive, large-scale transfers, contrary to its narrow scope.
assessment_rules.insufficient_evidence_when: It is unclear whether the company ever relies on this residual basis.

requirement_groups.principle: Restriction on public register derogation scope
requirement_groups.requirement_summary: Where the public-register derogation (49.1.g) is used, the transfer must not involve the entire register or entire categories of data, and if the register is limited to those with a legitimate interest, transfers should only be made at their request or to them as recipients.
requirement_groups.applicability_condition: Applies only where the company relies on the public register derogation in group 49.1 (sub-obligation 49.1.g).

sub_obligations.legal_text: A transfer...shall not involve the entirety of the personal data or entire categories of the personal data contained in the register. Where the register is intended for consultation by persons having a legitimate interest, the transfer shall be made only at the request of those persons or if they are to be the recipients
sub_obligations.plain_summary: Register-based transfers must be limited in scope and, for restricted-access registers, only made to or at the request of people with a legitimate interest.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Where the register derogation is used, does the policy confirm transfers are limited to less than the entire register/category and, for restricted registers, only made at the requester's initiative or to them as recipient?

assessment_rules.met_when: The single sub-obligation is satisfied: register transfers are scope-limited and restricted appropriately.
assessment_rules.partially_met_when: Scope limitation is mentioned generally but not tied to the specific restrictions required.
assessment_rules.not_met_when: Register-based transfers are made without any stated scope limitation.
assessment_rules.conflicting_when: The policy describes transferring an entire register or entire data category under this derogation.
assessment_rules.insufficient_evidence_when: It is unclear whether the register derogation is used at all.

requirement_groups.principle: Documentation duty for derogation-based transfers
requirement_groups.requirement_summary: The controller or processor must document the assessment and suitable safeguards for the residual compelling-legitimate-interest transfers in its Article 30 records.
requirement_groups.applicability_condition: Applies only where the company relies on the residual compelling-legitimate-interest basis (group 49.1.residual).

sub_obligations.legal_text: The controller or processor shall document the assessment as well as the suitable safeguards referred to in the second subparagraph of paragraph 1 of this Article in the records referred to in Article 30
sub_obligations.plain_summary: This particular assessment and its safeguards must be recorded in the company's Article 30 records of processing activities.
sub_obligations.evidence_prompt: Does the policy confirm that residual-basis transfer assessments and safeguards are documented in the Article 30 records of processing activities?

expected_evidence: Records of processing activities (Article 30 register) entry for the relevant transfer

assessment_rules.met_when: The single sub-obligation is satisfied: the relevant assessment and safeguards are documented within the Article 30 records.
assessment_rules.partially_met_when: An assessment exists but is not integrated into the Article 30 records.
assessment_rules.not_met_when: No documentation of the assessment exists anywhere.
assessment_rules.conflicting_when: Not applicable to this group.
assessment_rules.insufficient_evidence_when: It cannot be determined whether the residual basis is used, so the documentation duty's applicability is unclear.

chapter.name: Transfers of personal data to third countries or international organisations

article.title: International cooperation for the protection of personal data
article.contextual_reason: Article 50 addresses steps the European Commission and supervisory authorities take to build international cooperation, mutual assistance, and enforcement mechanisms between regulators. It does not impose any obligation on a controller or processor, so it has no corresponding requirement that can be tested against a company privacy policy.

article.title: Supervisory authority
article.contextual_reason: This article obliges Member States to establish independent supervisory authorities and governs how multiple authorities within a state coordinate and notify the Commission. It creates no obligation for a controller or processor, so it cannot be tested against a company privacy policy.

article.title: Independence
article.contextual_reason: This article requires Member States to guarantee the independence, staffing, and budget of their supervisory authorities. It regulates the state's relationship with its regulator, not a controller's or processor's conduct, so it is not testable against a company privacy policy.

article.title: General conditions for the members of the supervisory authority
article.contextual_reason: This article sets Member State rules for appointing, qualifying, and dismissing supervisory authority members. It has no bearing on controller or processor obligations and cannot be assessed against a company privacy policy.

article.title: Rules on the establishment of the supervisory authority
article.contextual_reason: This article requires Member States to legislate the establishment, appointment procedures, term length, and professional secrecy duties of supervisory authority members and staff. It imposes no requirement on controllers or processors and is not testable against a company privacy policy.

article.title: Competence
article.contextual_reason: This article allocates territorial jurisdiction between supervisory authorities and excludes courts acting in a judicial capacity from their supervision. It governs regulator jurisdiction, not controller or processor conduct, so it cannot be tested against a company privacy policy.

article.title: Competence of the lead supervisory authority

requirement_groups.principle: Identification of the lead supervisory authority for cross-border processing
requirement_groups.requirement_summary: A controller or processor carrying out cross-border processing should identify, and hold itself accountable to, the supervisory authority of its main or single EU establishment as its lead supervisory authority and sole interlocutor for that processing.
requirement_groups.applicability_condition: Applies only to controllers or processors that carry out cross-border processing (processing affecting data subjects in more than one Member State, or occurring in establishments in more than one Member State).

sub_obligations.legal_text: the supervisory authority of the main establishment or of the single establishment of the controller or processor shall be competent to act as lead supervisory authority for the cross-border processing
